Great walking in the fresh temperatures. A long but pretty easy and scenic descent to our lunch spot refugio d'Alos with amazing Spanish omlet and Gaspachio. Super nice people and a cute little town. Maybe a bit late in the day but happy we started our 700m ascent in the heat. Beginning was super steep then more shallow in the shade. We finally have horses again. Even on our camp spot. So curious they almost ate or sleeping pad and Rosa's socks drying on a tree branch. Relaxed afternoon with mountain scenery. ==> Happy. 😉

Day 29 We got another early start today. Good as it gave us shadow for almost all our climbing. It is only 6km to our next hut, but it is very rocky and very steep. Routefinding was involved and down climbing reasonably risky. While beautiful scenery was all around, with lakes and amazing rock shapes and colors, the going was very slow and tiring. 5h for 6km. At our little Refugio Pujol, we left or Backpacks and hiked up to a nice view point. The ridge for me, the summit for Rosa and Ryan. Amazing all around view, into France and into Spain. I could see way into the plains of France. Grand view for sure, seeing the difference between Spanish and French Pyrenees. Because of the clouds, I will try again to sleep in the Refugio. So far, almost all the attempts ended with me escaping to the outside anyway. So let's see. Day 30 The night was good and not too warm, none snored. We did our first departure without breakfast. It worked well. 1.5h into the walk we had breakfast next to a Cabana. A gentle descent through pleasant mixed tree forest. Loved it. Our lunch spot was combined with a lake dip, so so rejuvenating. The last climb to the pass went bye quickly, Funk went to the summit Rosa and I bailed on this and went straight to the hut for a beer and camp site search. Apparently the bunk beds in this (Certascan) hut are super tightly spaced. Food and staff were excellent and we had a good time talking to a group of Belgians. There was drinking too. Ryan spent some more time with them and had trouble finding the tent site.... But persistence prevailed.

Day 31 A great night outside. Some rain, lightning and wind, but nothing serious. Apparently we might have to expect similar weather the next 2-3 days. Not bad having a little cool down. We started 7.30 in some clouds and also blue sky. The scenery was superb coming down and looking back at the hut. The reservoir spewed it enormous amounts of water and made noise in accordance with it. A nice little climb to the opposite side of the valley made for great visuals too. As we dove into the next valley, there was silence, all of a sudden. No sound from the water, just silence. The view was stunning into the new lake and valley. What a beauty. Slightly downhill and pleasant. A tiny rock climbing passage to follow before we moved on to the new and bigger valley which demanded long whacky traverses over tall grasses and bushels, through trees. The only positive thing during all this traverse episode were the blueberries left and right on the trail. Tony but sorry tasteful. A little blueberry taste explosion in our mouths. This must have been the lowlight of all traverses I have ever done. Not at all a pleasant walk. This was followed by a step decent through the forest. In parts I felt like in Casentino Valley (my home) when I lost my path. After finishing 1000m descent we finally crossed the river and started our 1000m climb. Fortunately the trail was excellent and stunningly beautiful. We were treated to a lunch spot with waterfall shower. What a super treat. The rest of the ascent was just as comfortable to manage. Just that we saw a young Spanish man walking down really really slowly, with two other men on his side. He had a bandage on his head and leg. They said they do not need any help, so we walked on with even more care and a humbled mind. Don't forget to be careful with every step. We managed to be the first at the hut, only Max was already there, sleeping the whole morning. It is very very windy here, unusual..... Let's see what the next days bring. Ooooh, super surprise. Kilian and Katie arrived at 20.30 at our little hut. They caught me peeing..... It is so nice to see these two again. It looks like the trail provides. Day 32 We left without breakfast again. I like it a lot this way. The scenery in the morning was superb, the lake and the mountains around us. Then came the first group of kids, up the mountain. Probably 25-30 of them with I think teachers. Then another adult hiking group, then a women hiking group,.... Then then, in the end probably more than 50 people walked up to the lake this morning. Slow, but the first we had in many days. A quick note to Muriel to say I am ok. Then we had to climb the daily ~1000m up. The large valley offered amazingly beautiful views. Then down the pass again traversing to a spectacular valley and huge block of a mountain. Very impressive. After a short walk on a gravel road we are on a trail again and move up the 300m quickly to our lake and camping spot. Cleaning, then dinner with amazing Spanish Jamon. 🍖. An Australian young guy asked if he could join us and we had our usual dish, but with much entertainment. Good evening. Then, at almost 21.00 our two German friends came in. Super nice. The clouds provide an amazing spectacle moving in and around us here. Tomorrow should be a short day, but let's see. Day 33 It was a reasonably short day and we enjoyed it mostly together. A different day for all of us. We climbed up steeply again in the morning before breakfast then descended to a ski resort. Impressions on Blinkist APP and reading the Book ORWELL 1984

I signed up to Blinkist, an Audible book APP that condenses non-fiction books

![ORWELL1984](/photos/orwell1984.png)

to its essence and saves me a good amount of time and offers me a valuable service.

I recently read/listened to "ORWL 1984" . A book that was published 1994.  I thought of this book to be so bad, the message outdated and uninformed that I wrote the service.

This is what I wrote.

* * *

I just finished this short summary and have to say this is the most short sighted and not current summary of yours I have heard so far. I don't know if it is there book itself or your summary but at a minimum it is not up to the current knowledge and current starter in many countries. I would invite a review of this contribution.

If you want I can give a large number of examples to my opinion.

Thanks Stefan

* * *

**Response:**

May 3, 12:40 CEST

Hi Stefan,

Thanks for writing in your feedback.

When blinking a book we have decided to stick with the author's opinion stated in the book, even when it contains some contentious claims. I understand that it might be frustrating for some very committed readers with a lot of specialized knowledge, but we try to choose the books featured in our app very carefully and on strong grounds. Please note that the lack of currency in the book's content might be easily explained with the fact that the book was released in 1994.

Since the idea of Blinkist is to offer the big ideas from non-fiction books in a compact format, most important thing for us is to stay true to the original book. I hope you understand :)

Feel free to contact us again if you should have any other suggestions or questions.

All the best, Gi..........

* * *

**My response:**

Thanks for your response. I appreciate it.

I understand the release date hinders the author of "current" knowledge. YOU, however, as Blinkist, seem to carry a responsibility in the release of books as well, just by which books you offer to your current clients. In my view, this very book about Orwell 1984, and it's conclusions are very out of date and lead to conclusions that were correct at the time, best case, un-informed and without significant foresight more realistically.

**YOUR** selection to place this book on your Blinkist Platform and make this obviously outdated information easily available to a large number of people is what I see as irresponsible.

It brings up concerns in my mind how much I should trust your selection process and truly reduces the value Blinkist brings to me.

I value what you do, condensing non-fiction books into the essence. I expect the information presented to me to be current. I understand the topic of this very book well and could reject the outdated content. I would like to convince Blinkist to protect me from wrong, outdated information in areas where I am not as informed.

Am I expecting something unreasonable?

Thanks for your time.

Stefan

Intensity - German acceleration and a lot of beauty - right here in Tuscany

In all this whirlwind of impressions, rushing here for a house viewing, driving there to check out a new village, coming back for a visit with a contractor, saying thanks with some homemade bread..... Here in Tuscany there always seems enough time for a great experience.

**Eating a salad**, with stuff we bought in just a simple market brings out flavors that I almost forgot. Thin Fennel slices that have an intensity of taste, chicory leaves that have no problem standing out in the flavor profile, green lettuce that is actually crunchy, olive oil that actually tastes like olives. These are not so subtle reminders of what food can taste like if it is grown well, harvested when it is ripe and brought to the market the next day for you to buy.

**Eating meat**, prepared with just salt and some herbs, grilled to perfection. The portions that we got did not breach the side of our plates but were just as much as I could or wanted to eat. The juices of this orchestra were few but delicious. The Restaurant was 3-4km out of Arrezo in the hills. Unassuming and family owned since 50+ years. The service was personal, fast and heartfelt. There was nothing even remotely fake about this afternoon.

**The drive** there was exhilarating as we were driven by our newly made friends  Roberto and Grazia. I never sat in a Porche SUV, and I certainly now understand that some automatic transmissions are made for a truly sportive drive and is made in perfection. A safe and smooth ride thanks to some German engineering greatness.

**Listening.** I don't really understand Italian yet. But you don't really have to, to feel the intensity and experience the way communication seems to be done here. There never is a business only conversation, as it seems to me. There is always time for a heartfelt chit-chat and seeing how the other is really doing. Talking with your hands is mandatory as it seems, talking quietly seems like an insult. Emotions are always a big part of communication and you feel it.

Google photos [LINK](https://photos.app.goo.gl/Aw6rkg7UAekoxr898) ### English After our flight from Sucre to la Paz we did not spend any time in town but headed right to Copacabana. No, not the famous beach in Rio but the little town next to lake Titicaca. It's more of a transit town for us tourists and not to much to do there really. Apart from a pretty unique church in town there is not much beauty around. We took the time and visited the very worthy poncho museum in town. I know, it does not sound like much but it was really well done and informative. Isla del Sole is a1 1/2 hour boat ride (slow slow boat ride) and there is no motorized transportation on the island. It's very scenic with reasonable climate, warm during the day and windier, colder after dinner. Some of the views offered during dinner on the patio are really amazing. Only till about two years ago one could do a hike from the south end to the north and back. We wanted to do it and had to find out the locals no longer want tourists walking in the area coming from South of the island. The reason seems to be money. The South, where we went, is pretty much setup for tourists with Accommodation and restaurants. A super welcoming, respectful, inquisitive barista and his helper kept us in the place for at least 1/2h 45min. We got to understand his family history, marital situation, places he lived in and with whom, how long, and why. We spoke about our lively travels through life as well and we had another "_welcome to Napoli_" behind us.  > What is happening here? Though we wanted to go and have a light dinner, we decided, enough is enough and we went to bed. Breakfast was served by Patrizia, and it came with many more tips and details about her life and her city. Incredible. How caring and communicative can someone be? We were the last people permitted to have a delicious lunch that day at this restaurant. But the Boss almost exactly told us what to order, and why. It's not a big deal, it's a HUGE deal - our visit in Ashland

Google Pictures [LINK](https://photos.app.goo.gl/BZWjQNCM9ZdX9hHs6)

As we now have our San Jose house on the market for sale, we are making some use of this time to the country we are about to leave as well as visiting "**fellow Bay Area exiters**". Our friends the Kuwabaras moved to Ashland Oregon and they were nice enough to host us for a week. Seeing them and seeing Ashland was great. What topped it off seeing and being with them and their kids is not something we have done before and it was "**not a big deal, it's a HUGE deal**", as Nikko, their youngest son coined a new phrase for us.

Moving into the home Yu grew up in after doing some pretty intense overhauling seems like a great thing to do and they did that while living in their Van for a while, then moving in as the work goes on. Ashland is an interesting town in the south of Oregon, in the middle of some amazing mid-sized mountains. A University, small stores and interesting places to be and stay, parks and what seems like a pretty amazing sense of community in this town. Yu and I made some good use of the weather to get out on a MTB ride, except I used my Brompton for it and seem to live to talk about it.

![IMG\_8578](/photos/img_8578.jpg)

We followed it up with a hike through the hills with Mumu to the town of Ashland. They really have a good playground here, right in front of their doorstep.

\

There is Mount "A" withing 30min drive and it offers plenty of SKi fun for all levels and community fun in the hut with music, food, and drinks. It's even ok to bring your own food and drinks there, as long as you show up and be part of the fun. The Ski area is now owned by the city of Ashland and just needs to break even in terms of financing. What a difference that makes to the people that come and the climate you create in a Ski hut. I love the idea and loved it there.

One trip to Crater Lake with Yu renewed my love for this place. It's simple and there is not so much to do in winter unless you take skies and hike along the rim, from one peak to the next. But it is amazing and impressive, spiritual and beautiful. Crater lake was formed from a much taller Vulcano that spewed out so much lava that the top, now nothing more than a shell collapsed and created a concave  structure, now the Crater lake.

![DSC05030-S](/photos/dsc05030-s.jpg)

We got to meet some of their childhood friends one evening ina Potluck. These guys, I think, choose a good spot to move to.

We moved on to Portland for a few days and meet up with Janel and Chris who are feeling out, if exiting the Bay Are towards Portland is what they want to do. We are more than glad in assisting this process a little with some bike trips in the area and some beer tasting. I want to be really sure we do thorough testing.

But already on the first night, our little Fiat 500 showed signs of weakness and refused to start. I will have to look into what the problem might be.

Its so hard to get to easy

GOOGLE Pictures [LINK](https://photos.app.goo.gl/gETMoqsW8RR7czmQ9)

I am not really complaining with this post. I am just expressing my amazement. Amazed about the amount of effort it takes to move one's life. The whole life I mean. All the stuff you own, all the things you take for granted being where you are, the insurances, the bank accounts, the car, the supermarket you know, the hardware store you know, the pastry shop you found giving you exactly the type of smile you want on a Saturday after getting up late and you take what you deserve and what you deserve is an easy day with a coffee and a good pastry in the sun, maybe with a friend. Your bicycle supply shop, the bicycle repair guy, the location where you buy motor oil, get your pictures framed, buy your insurance, the place where you can go and ask for help at the city, ..... You know, stuff you need to support real life. Everyday items and locations, people, information. We need so so much, some of it every day, some only once a year. But we do know where to do it and how to do it, we also usually speak the language. For Mumu and me, none of that was true when we started this gigantic project of moving our life to Italy and moved it to a rural area, in that rural area we moved to a pretty remote location.

We now have moved in the house since October and I could not be more grateful. I mean that. It feels so so good to have walls around you that you know will not change. We are located in an area where we can walk out of the gates and be in nature. I have that super high on my list of appreciative things, for sure. Starting to get the legs back into a little bit of shape is needed and feels good, doing that in an environment so beautiful and plentiful as here and as close is super. And my mind is on an easier track now than during March-April of the year. But I have to say, some days I am still in crisis mode and my head does not seem to empty of things I really need to do or get done, EVER. I am not myself in terms of being the open and creative solution finder that I usually am. I have blinds on and miss easy solutions, make things harder than they need to be, ...... I am not in a quiet mind set. YET. I would love to get there soon!!

All this is just to realize how much it takes to truly move one's life. I did not expect this.

In the meantime, we are able to see and discover our area pretty well. We managed to pick one of the coldest days to go up the mountain to see Eremo di Camaldoli again, and it ended up being -5 to -10C up there. COOOLD. We did not bring quiet the right clothing for this, but we just hiked a little faster and we stayed warm(ish). It is rewarding to me seeing nature change in the seasons. In another 4 months it will have been one year we got to experience this place, right here. It s such an interesting mix of personalities here.

I cleared my mountain bike from all the spiderwebs, go the tubeless tires back in working condition and set out to start the process of "**G**etting **M**y **L**egs **B**ack" (GMLB). I know it will take a few months, to catch up again to the state I was in towards the beginning of the year, or even middle of last year. It's humbling and it is still fun. I also need this time by myself for mental recovery. I feel so much better after only 1.5 or 2 hours ride. And riding now means on the mountain bike. The road bike is too cold for me on many days. Then it means to start riding from the house, straight on the trails and into our forest. It is a mud bath, many days and my bike as well as I need a good shower after. COVID is not a real restriction in this regard as I usually meet none on the rides. There is no Police to check, but also really no reason to check as I am just as alone here as in the house.

I made a longer set of pictures which starts from signing the contract to buy the house, going to California, selling the house, see you later to many of our friends, to confinement in Germany and then the process of remodeling the house and land till today. [LINK](https://photos.app.goo.gl/e15xKUyFcKxpY6VM6)

To come back to the original topic of this post, getting to the "easy" way of living. I find it hard and I need to bring out a lot of effort, planning and doing, to finally get to the easy and grounded life I am looking for. I learned to appreciate the planning and action it takes for people that look like they do have an easy life now. Smart decisions will have been made. And what we see is "easy". If anyone found an easy way to EASY, please let me know.

Jul 16 ---- 2018 SASC CHAIRMAN JOHN McCAIN ON TRUMP-PUTIN MEETING

I am re-posting this statement from John Mc Cain. I am by no means a fan of John, but he is one of the few politicians that have a spine and have a brain (a dying breed sadly).

Source: [LINK](https://www.mccain.senate.gov/public/index.cfm/2018/7/statement-by-sasc-chairman-john-mccain-on-trump-putin-meeting)

**_Washington, D.C._** – U.S. Senator John McCain (R-AZ), Chairman of the Senate Armed Services Committee, released the following statement today on President Trump’s meeting and press conference with Vladimir Putin in Helsinki:

“Today’s press conference in Helsinki was one of the most disgraceful performances by an American president in memory. The damage inflicted by President Trump’s naiveté, egotism, false equivalence, and sympathy for autocrats is difficult to calculate. But it is clear that the summit in Helsinki was a tragic mistake.

“President Trump proved not only unable, but unwilling to stand up to Putin. He and Putin seemed to be speaking from the same script as the president made a conscious choice to defend a tyrant against the fair questions of a free press, and to grant Putin an uncontested platform to spew propaganda and lies to the world.

“It is tempting to describe the press conference as a pathetic rout – as an illustration of the perils of under-preparation and inexperience. But these were not the errant tweets of a novice politician. These were the deliberate choices of a president who seems determined to realize his delusions of a warm relationship with Putin’s regime without any regard for the true nature of his rule, his violent disregard for the sovereignty of his neighbors, his complicity in the slaughter of the Syrian people, his violation of international treaties, and his assault on democratic institutions throughout the world.

“Coming close on the heels of President Trump’s bombastic and erratic conduct towards our closest friends and allies in Brussels and Britain, today’s press conference marks a recent low point in the history of the American Presidency. That the president was attended in Helsinki by a team of competent and patriotic advisors makes his blunders and capitulations all the more painful and inexplicable.

“No prior president has ever abased himself more abjectly before a tyrant. Not only did President Trump fail to speak the truth about an adversary; but speaking for America to the world, our president failed to defend all that makes us who we are—a republic of free people dedicated to the cause of liberty at home and abroad. American presidents must be the champions of that cause if it is to succeed. Americans are waiting and hoping for President Trump to embrace that sacred responsibility. One can only hope they are not waiting totally in vain.”

Wir haben hier mit unserem Hotel Gold geschlagen, neue, nette, junge Leute (nicht wir) und ein tolles Zimmer. Wir gingen in den Gion District, einen älteren Stadtteil mit vielen historischen Gebäuden, Tempeln und Schreinen,…

Mit Mumu für 30 km durch Kyoto radeln, um eine weitere Ablehnung für die Übersetzung meines deutschen Führerscheins zu erhalten (in Japan das Recht zu leihen und ein Auto zu fahren). Das Radfahren entlang des Flusses Katzua war ordentlich, da es uns einen kleinen Blick auf ein bewohnbares Kyoto gab. Wir sahen Leute, die ein Spiel im Chrokee-Stil spielten, nur dass sie einen gefiederten Ball verwendeten, ähnlich, aber größer als Badminton. Das Ziel scheint zu sein, es in einen großen Korb zu bringen,…. Geheimnisvoll Bamboo Gardens, Ryōan-ji Zen Garden und wir machten uns auf den Weg zurück in die Stadt.

Wir sahen Leute, die ein gefiedertes Ballspiel spielten. Was ist das???? Es ist NICHT das hier.

Ich habe hier viel guten Kaffee gefunden. Hmmmm. In japanischer Perfektion gemacht. Eines Nachmittags sind wir in ein kleines Restaurant im japanischen Stil “gestoßen” - insgesamt 10 Plätze, sehr einfache Einrichtung und einfache Einrichtung. Das Essen, das wir präsentierten, war für mich aber einfach. Ein Zehn-Kurs, und jeder war neues Essen für mich. Der einzige Kurs, den ich aussprechen kann, ist “Cherry Blossom Sake”.

Während wir uns in Japan auf die Goldene Woche einlassen, wird die Unterkunft knapp, und wir mussten aus unserem Hotel ausziehen und weiter nach Norden in Kyoto in ein privat geführtes BnB ziehen. Wir waren in einem traditionellen Zimmer untergebracht, im Wesentlichen ohne Möbel und nur zwei Matratzen im Tatame-Stil, die mit unseren Bettlaken und Kissen auf dem Boden aufgerollt waren. Es kam mir seltsam vor, diesen Raum zu betreten, so ungewöhnlich. Alles ist sauber und stilvoll, aber für mich war es immer noch seltsam. Dies ist ein leerer Raum. Japan ist so anders.

Wir fanden eine erstaunliche Bäckerei (Tom Sawyer) in dieser Wohngegend sowie ein wirklich süßes Kaffeehaus, das aus einem öffentlichen Badehaus umgebaut wurde. Wirklich cool.

Wir mussten die berühmten Tore hier sehen. Die Tori-Tore [[to.ɾi.i]) ist ein traditionelles japanisches Tor, das am häufigsten am Eingang eines Shinto-Schreins oder in einem Shinto-Schrein zu finden ist, wo es symbolisch den Übergang vom Leichen zum Heiligen darstellt.

Samurai in der japanischen Kultur. Ich war misstrauisch Waren diese berühmten Krieger hier so wichtig? Oder waren sie eher ein vorübergehendes Phänomen wie die USA mit ihren Cowboys. Nach nicht mehr als 50-100 Jahren war alles vorbei. …… .. Nein, die Samurai sind sehr real in der Geschichte. Sie scheinen seit ~ 1100 Jahren als eine Art Söldnerkrieger zu existieren. Erst im 19. Jahrhundert scheinen sich die Samurai in das Gefüge einer „normalen“ Gesellschaft zu integrieren. Einige Samurai wurden Geschäftsleute. So gründete Iwasaki Yatarō, der Urenkel eines Samurai, Mitsubishi. Lesen Sie hier mehr über diese faszinierende Klasse.

Danke an Mumu, dass ich mir einige Bilder für diesen Blog ausleihen durfte. Nicht nur heute, sondern in fast allen meinen Beiträgen. Küsse.

Après seulement deux nuits à Tokyo, nous avons quitté cette ville immense. Le train Shinkansen, ce train ultra-rapide, propre et élégant nous y conduit. J’étais surpris de devoir acheter un billet physique, de le faire envoyer à la poste (à côté de la gare) et de récupérer le billet pour pouvoir utiliser ce fantastique service. Pas de possibilité d’avoir un service de billetterie électronique dans ce pays sophistiqué. Il m’a fallu environ 45 minutes pour trouver le bureau de poste, trouver la file d’attente où je puisse aller le chercher, remplir le formulaire nécessaire pour le récupérer et retrouver mon chemin pour retrouver Mumu qui attendait avec les sacs. Dans un style japonais discipliné, nous avons trouvé l’équipe de nettoyage et le personnel de sécurité des portes en ordre et en ordre, attendant le train et entrant pour le nettoyer, puis faire notre rapport à la fin du travail.

C’est incroyable pour moi de voir ça. Presque comme un spectacle, mais ce n’est pas. La plupart des choses sont très disciplinées et ordonnées ici. Il y a beaucoup de règles, et presque toutes seront suivies par presque tout le monde. Je recommande d’arriver tôt à la gare et de faire la queue si vous avez un billet sans assignation de siège. Trois minutes après que nous ayons choisi notre siège, presque toutes les places étaient occupées, cinq minutes après notre arrivée, nous quittions la gare pour nous rendre à Kyoto. C’était lisse, à l’heure, confortable et efficace. Même à 270 km / h, nous avions le WiFi, de superbes vues sur le mont Fuji et des paysages magnifiques.

Nous avons trouvé l’or avec notre hôtel ici, neuf, mignon, les jeunes (pas nous) et une grande salle. Nous nous sommes dirigés vers le quartier de Gion, un quartier de la ville plus ancienne avec de nombreux bâtiments historiques et des temples et…

Parcourir Kyoto avec Mumu pendant 30 km à vélo, un autre refus de la traduction de mon permis de conduire allemand (être autorisé à louer et conduire une voiture au Japon). Faire du vélo le long de la rivière Katzua était super, car cela nous donnait une petite vue sur un Kyoto vivable. Nous avons vu des gens jouer à un jeu de style Chrokee, mais ils utilisaient simplement un ballon à plumes, similaire mais plus gros que le badminton. Le but semble être de le mettre dans un grand panier,…. Mystérieux. Bamboo Gardens, Ryōan-ji Zen Garden et nous sommes retournés en ville.

Nous avons vu des gens jouer à un jeu de balle à plumes. Qu’est-ce que c’est???? Ce n’est PAS celui-ci

J’ai trouvé beaucoup de bon café ici. Hmmmm. Fait à la perfection japonaise. Un déjeuner, nous avons «rencontré» un petit restaurant de style japonais - 10 places au total, une configuration très basique et un établissement simple. La nourriture que nous avons présentée était tout sauf simple pour moi. Un cours de dix, et chacun était nouvelle nourriture pour moi. Le seul cours que je peux prononcer est «Saké à la fleur de cerisier».

Alors que nous entrons dans la Golden Week ici au Japon, le logement devient serré et nous avons dû quitter notre hôtel pour nous déplacer plus au nord de Kyoto dans une BnB privée. Nous étions logés dans une chambre traditionnelle, avec essentiellement pas de meubles et seulement deux matelas de style Tatame, roulés sur le sol avec nos draps et nos oreillers. C’était étrange pour moi d’entrer dans cette pièce si inhabituelle. Tout est propre et élégant, mais c’était quand même étrange pour moi. C’est une pièce vide. Le Japon est tellement différent.

Nous avons trouvé une boulangerie extraordinaire (Tom Sawyer) dans ce quartier résidentiel ainsi qu’un café vraiment mignon qui a été reconçu à partir d’un bain public. Vraiment cool.

Nous devions aller voir les célèbres portes ici. Les portes de Tori. [[to.ɾi.i]) est une porte japonaise traditionnelle que l’on trouve le plus souvent à l’entrée ou dans un sanctuaire shinto, où elle marque symboliquement la transition du mondain au sacré]

Samouraï dans la culture japonaise. J’étais méfiant. Ces guerriers célèbres étaient-ils si importants ici? Ou étaient-ils plutôt un phénomène temporaire comme ce que les États-Unis ont avec leurs Cowboys. Tout était fini après pas plus de 50-100 ans. …… .. Non, les samouraïs sont très réels dans l’histoire. Ils semblent exister depuis environ 1100 ans en tant que guerrier mercenaire. Ce n’est qu’au XIXe siècle que les samouraïs semblent s’intégrer à la société «normale». Certains samouraïs sont devenus des hommes d’affaires. Par exemple, Iwasaki Yatarō, l’arrière-petit-fils d’un samouraï, a créé Mitsubishi. Plus de lecture ici sur cette classe fascinante.

Merci à Mumu de m’avoir laissé emprunter certaines de ses photos pour ce blog. Pas seulement aujourd’hui, mais dans presque tous mes messages. Des bisous.

Ce que j’ai entendu et que j’ai entendu dire, c’est de sous-traiter le travail nécessaire pour vivre, d’enseigner durement à l’université locale et de surfer sur le reste du temps ou sur quelques autres goûts d’équilibre travail-vie personnelle. Miles et miles de l'attitude de l'entreprise de style de Tokyo. Le lendemain matin, nous partons dans le sud pour rencontrer des amis de Rebecca sur la plage pour une journée de camping. Quel excellent groupe d'amis a Rebecca. Un mélange de hollandais et de japonais, fondé et ouvert, naturellement amical et lié à la nature et à la personne qui lui est proche. Une expérience formidable. Hiroka, Alex et Yoshi. Un autre Onsen et nous avons réussi à y rencontrer un développeur Web français. La chance l’avait et j’aurais la chance de faire du vélo avec Jérôme le lendemain matin. 60 km 1000m, 2,5 heures. Pas mal sur un VTT. COURT Vidéo de moi avec Jérôme Une autre promenade avec Rebecca et Mumu à Aoshima le long de la plage nous a offert une vue sur un navire récemment coulé. (un capitaine alcoolique était la cause apparente). Nous devions déterminer le besoin absolu d'un permis de conduire international pour pouvoir conduire une voiture au Japon. OU vous avez comme moi un DL allemand. Vous pouvez le faire traduire dans un bureau JAF local (pensez à AAA ou ADAC), et vous êtes prêt à partir. Mais je ne l'avais pas avec moi, bien sûr. Nous avons donc envoyé notre licence à Céline, via FedEx. Aucun problème. Sauf que c'était la Golden Week. Au 1er lundi de mai. FedEx a indiqué qu'il ne serait pas en mesure de livrer avant mardi, au plus tôt. Mais nous sommes au Japon ici, les choses fonctionnent différemment, les gens travaillent plus dur ici, et ils orthographient bien le service, je pense uniquement en caractères gras. La première tentative de livraison a eu lieu vendredi. C'est au milieu de la semaine d'or. Nous n'étions même pas encore à la maison. Elle a donc été livrée lundi, le dernier jour des jours fériés les plus importants au Japon. Je ai été impressionné. Vraiment impressionné. Ainsi, tous nos projets initiaux pouvaient encore avancer et Rebecca, la gentille personne qu'elle était, nous a conduits au bureau de la JAF sur le chemin du travail, risquant d’être en retard pour sa conférence (mais l’ayant quand même fait). 1/2 heure avant l'ouverture, le bureau était déjà rempli de tous les travailleurs. Un homme, nous voyant à l'extérieur, est sorti et s'est excusé pour ne pas être encore ouvert et est retourné à son bureau. 9.00 et nous étions le 1er là-bas et les seuls là-bas. 1/2 heure de paperasse, 1 heure d'attente et nous avions le document traduit nécessaire. IMPRESSIONNANT. Off à la voiture de location de budget où la voiture nous attendait déjà. MAIS, ce ne sont pas les États-Unis où vous venez de sauter dans la voiture et aller. La paperasse est essentielle ici. J'ai donc rempli et signé aux bons endroits, suivi des consignes de sécurité, suivi un petit cours de code de la route, puis visionné en toute sécurité la vidéo au Japon sur une minuscule tablette à l'intérieur d'un livret, créé uniquement à cet effet. Les Japonais essaient d'empêcher leurs clients de faire des erreurs et de se blesser. OK, maintenant je suis assis dans la voiture et je pars. NON, nous devons inspecter le véhicule à la recherche de rayures minuscules et d'éventuelles imperfections. OK, maintenant je suis assis dans la voiture et je pars. NON, le système de navigation est uniquement en japonais et alors seulement, je pourrais descendre dans les rues. Je n'étais pas du tout ennuyé par cela. J'aime quand les gens sont approfondis pour de bonnes raisons. Peu effrayant sur le côté gauche de la route, mais ça allait. Trois heures à travers la magnifique campagne verdoyante et fantastique ainsi que dans la région montagneuse et nous nous trouvons à Takachiho. Eh bien, pas exactement. Nous avons eu un autre (de trop déjà) des incidents de guidage de Google Maps. Nous nous sommes retrouvés du mauvais côté de la petite montagne et nous nous sommes retrouvés au milieu de nulle part, mais tout seuls et ils devaient avoir l'air plutôt pitoyables. Nous avons fini par montrer la photo de notre «hôtel de style temple» au facteur local. Il se gratta la tête pendant un moment, puis sauta sur son petit scooter et se dirigea devant nous. Il nous a fallu au moins 10 minutes pour y arriver et il a fait tout son possible pour nous aider à trouver où nous devions aller. Quelle culture, quel homme. Comment est-ce génial? Mumu et moi avons sauté de la voiture et lui avons longuement serré la main. WOW, j'ai été impressionné. Essayez cela en France ou en Allemagne. Essayez cela aux États-Unis et vous ne recevrez pas ce service. "Dogeza." Nous sommes arrivés dans notre nouvelle maison pour quatre nuits. Un vrai bijou dans la région. Une famille de deux prêtres Yoshimura qui ont construit une loge juste à côté de leur temple. Le petit village semble concentré sur l'agriculture, le paysage vert et magnifique. J'ai trouvé la finition extérieure de la loge inhabituelle, le bardage de bois brûlé / carbonisé. Ça a l'air génial, mais qu'est-ce que c'est, pourquoi le faire. C'est une ancienne manière japonaise traditionnelle de construire. Yakisugi (杉) est une méthode japonaise traditionnelle de préservation du bois. Yaki signifie chauffer au feu, et sugi est un cyprès. … En carbonisant légèrement la surface du bois sans brûler toute la pièce, le bois devient imperméable à l'eau par la carbonisation et est donc plus durable. Il protège également contre les insectes. Voici quelques instructions de bricolage sur la façon de le faire. Mumu et moi sommes allés au GORGE bien sûr le 1er jour et c'était génial. Nous avons conduit au mont. Asu le lendemain, un jour de pluie et nous avons été récompensés par d'autres vues vertes magnifiques et une visite à Onsen. Puis il y avait la cabane dans les arbres, en fait je pense la mère de toutes les cabanes dans les arbres. Mère de toutes les cabanes dans les arbres

We took another Shinkansen train, fast, elegant, on-time and fabulous. We took it to an island Kyushu, that is so much non-japanese in my view. There are few corporations located here, and I don’t see any High Tech companies here, there is a lot of green and a lot of space on this island, villages, hiking paths in so many places, Beaches with surfers and the related people attracted to these beaches. We see hippie restaurants, campgrounds with musical jam sessions…. Don’t get me wrong, SUPER friendly island, incredible people. It’s just that many more here does not fit my expectation of Japan. But I am trying to learn.

Mumu and I were fortunate enough to be welcomed and picked up by Rebecca, the sister of Kimbo. She lives since 20+ years in different areas of Japan and seems to have integrated well. Right out of the regional train we met her in a small train station, where, I guess, middle of nowhere in Japan was defined.

A tour through some local sites included a beautiful waterfall and an Onsen (Japanese public Bathhouse) where we could eat, buy some locally grown produce and steam our eggs in the local geothermal steam. How awesome is that? Five minutes and, if you are careful, you get out your eggs without being burnt. No warning signs here (that I could read), you need to watch out what you are doing.

One tub of the Onsen was so hot. I came out with red skin only after 2-3 minutes in there. Locals stayed MUCH longer. We visited the local Beach scene in Aoshima and had a beer and the local version of Mexican Burritos. Not bad at all for being this far away. There is a lot of Surf activity here; a lot of people seem to make life work here. Work and play that is. Contracting as much work as needed to live, teaching hard at the local University and surfing the rest of the time or a few other flavors of work/life balance are what I heard of and saw. Miles and miles away from Tokyo-style corporate attitude. The next morning we go off to the south, to meet friends of Rebecca on the beach for a day of camping. What an excellent set of friends Rebecca has. A mix of Dutch and Japanese, grounded and open, naturally friendly and connected to nature and the person next to them. A great experience. Hiroka, Alex and Yoshi. Another Onsen and we managed to meet a French Web developer there. Luck had it, and I get to ride a bike with Jerome the next morning. 60km 1000m up, 2.5hours. Not bad on an MTB. SHORT Video of me with Jerome

Another ride with Rebecca and Mumu to Aoshima right along the beach offered us a view of a recently sunk ship. (an alcohol-impaired captain was the apparent cause).

We had to find out about the absolute need for an international drivers license to be allowed to operate a car in Japan. OR, you have like me, a German DL. You can get it translated at a local JAF office (think AAA or ADAC), and you are good to go. But I did not have it with me, of course. So we had our good friend Celine send the license via FedEx. No problem. Except it was Golden Week. To the 1st Monday in May. FedEx stated it would not be able to deliver before Tuesday, earliest. But we are in Japan here, things work different, people work harder here, and they spell service correctly, I think only in BOLD letters. The first delivery attempt was made Friday. That is in the middle of Golden Week. We were not even at the house yet. So it was delivered Monday, on the last day of the most important public holidays in Japan. I was impressed. Really impressed. So all our original plans could still move forward and Rebecca, the nice person she is, drove us to the JAF office on her way to work risking to be late for her lecture (but still made it). 1/2 hour before opening, the office was already filled with all the workers. One man, seeing us outside, came out and apologized for not being open yet and went back to his desk. 9.00 and we were the 1st there and only ones there. 1/2 hour paperwork, 1 hour waiting and we had the needed translated document. AWESOME. Off to Budget rental car where the car was waiting for us already. BUT, this is not the USA where you just jump into the car and go. Paperwork is vital here. So I filled and signed at the right places, was guided through safety documentation, took a little traffic rules class and then watched the drive safely in Japan video on a tiny tablet inside a booklet, made only for this purpose. Japanese are trying to preventing their customer from making mistakes and getting hurt. OK, Now I sit in the car and go. NO, we need to inspect the vehicle about scratches of minuscule sizes and any imperfections. OK, now I sit in the car and go. NO, the Navigation system is in Japanese only and then, only then I could hit the streets. I was not at all annoyed by it. I like it when people are thorough for good reasons. Little scary on the left side of the road, but I was ok. Three hours through the beautiful green and fantastic countryside and mountain style area and we ere in Takachiho. Well, not exactly. We had another one (of too many already) of the Google Maps misguiding incidents. We ended up on the wrong side of the small mountain and stood in the middle of nowhere again, but all alone and must have looked pretty pitiful. We ended up showing the picture of our “Temple style hotel” to the local postman. He scratched his head for a while, then hopped on his little scooter and drove in front of us to the place. It took us at least 10 minutes to get there, and he went way out of his way to help us find where we needed to go. What a culture, what a man. How awesome is that? Mumu and I jumped out of the car and shook his hand, long and well. WOW, I was impressed. Try that in France or Germany. Try that in the US, and you will not receive this service. “dogeza.”

We have arrived at our new home for four nights. A real Gem in the area. A family of two Pure Land Buddhist priests that built a lodge right next to their Temple. The little village seems focussed on agriculture, the scenery green and stunning. I found the outside finish of the lodge unusual, burnt/charred wood siding. It looks great, but what is it, why do it. It is an old traditional Japanese way to build.

_Yakisugi (焼杉) is a traditional Japanese method of wood preservation. Yaki means to heat with fire, and sugi is cypress. … By slightly charring the surface of the wood without combusting the whole piece, the wood becomes water-proof through the carbonisation and is thus more durable. It also protects against insects.

Wir sind für vier Nächte in unserem neuen Zuhause angekommen. Ein echtes Juwel in der Gegend. Eine Familie von zwei Yoshimura-Priestern, die direkt neben ihrem Tempel eine Lodge errichteten. Yakisugi (焼 杉) ist eine traditionelle japanische Methode des Holzschutzes. Es schützt auch vor Insekten.

Let's go on a company dinner - The Italian way

As many of you know, I am in the finishing stretch of remodeling our new home in Tuscany, Italy. People are passionate about their work here, diligent about doing the job right, on time and and and. Many of the stigma points I had of the Italian way to live, to be, to interact, to work proved to be not correct at all and that was a good thing. What might have helped is the fact that we moved to the Tuscany area. By many people here, it is considered the Switzerland of Italy. All I can say, what we were able to accomplish in 1 1/2 years is pretty amazing; I doubt I could have done that in Germany, I really do.

Now, I am a little off-topic I think. Last week, the team of the construction company wanted to get together for a dinner. NICE I thought. Then it became clear that I will be invited too. As I am such a big customer of theirs, they wanted to all see me as well. Speaking was not all that possible as I still only speak a very very small number of Italian words and it is pitiful to hear the stuff that comes out of my mouth that way. Nevertheless, they invited me. NICE move I thought. I was directed to the local watering hole, pizza place, and all together community hangout. The fact that they brew their own beer on the 1st floor, the restaurant is on the ground floor helps to make this a loved go-to place. Prices are reasonable, food is really good and plenty, service is good, people are friendly. Good place for a bigger get-together like they planned. 9 people in the company, 8 could make it.

When I arrive, I see some known faces, some new ones that do work behind the curtain for customers. I slowly figure out the mix of people. Some Italians, local from the Casentino Valley, some Albanians where I was quickly advised of the differences between northern and southern Albanian people. Then a few people from Romania and then me. Lots and lots of food was brought up to the table. People actually do physical work here, and you can see that they energize accordingly. The talking was plentiful, loud, and with plenty of passion. But what is never forgotten is the Italian politeness and respect for each other. While opinions are voiced without a hand in front of one's mouth; loud and clear, it is always done politely and in style. While I really could not understand most of what was said, it gave me the opportunity to look at the faces and non-verbal communication that went on. Fascinating. People liked each other and respected each other.

The boss of the company sat there, talked, and listened just like any of the rest. He was never treated in any way differently than anyone else. The respect he received, was given to everyone. Now here comes the deal. They sat together as a set of friends, for 3 hours, really having a good time seeing each other and talking it up. When it was time to leave, I mean, pay 1st, then leave, It was made clear to me, that I will not pay. Hmmm, OK. The good customer does not pay. I get it. Then I find out, not only does the boss not pay for all of us. No! He does not pay at all. The complete staff invites him (and me) for this dinner. The reason that was given to me was; he invited everyone last time, it was time to pay back. **SO**, not only did pretty much everyone come to the company event, they had a good time did not have to get bribed by a company T-Shirt and logo water bottle. Then to top it all off they each paid for the dinner for themself and for their boss.

\==> Italians seem to love life with others, they seem to need their friends around and are not shy to make new acquaintances quickly. To me, they are truly passionate people who do to want to disappoint. They are inclusive and very polite. Etiquette is a thing many know and act in accordance with. In an interesting twist, it seems to me that Italians are true individualists at heart, but do not want to miss the strong and tightly woven mesh of a social support network. There are no libertarians here that I know, only in the region of Livorno I have seen true socialists and even anarchists. There are not many extremes here, people stay more in the middle. I am so happy we moved here. Imagine, one day I will be able to speak their language and talk maybe 1/2 the speed they can. I would be up the moon and back.

Das Gebäude schien neu gebaut zu sein, und es war nicht viel für meinen Geschmack, es sah aus wie ein überladenes Interieur, keine einheitlichen Stile und alles zusammen ein wenig Schuhkarton. Die Cocktails waren lecker, aber ich liebte kein Essen. Es schien alles erzwungen zu sein und fehlte der wesentliche, GESCHMACK. Keine Raffinesse erforderlich, um erkannt zu werden. Nur eine gute Kreation war das, was ich von einem Ort wie diesem erwartet habe. Nicht süß, nicht salzig, nur gute Würze und eine Erfindung fehlte. Unsere beiden Hauptgerichte waren einfach großartig und mein Nachtisch war einfach schlecht. Daumen runter.

Peru und Kartoffeln. Ich hatte keine Ahnung, wie zentrisch Kartoffeln zu peruanischem Essen sind. Es gibt mehr als 330 Kartoffelsorten. Wir hatten einige davon; einige sind den Typen ähnlich, die ich vorher hatte; Einige konnte ich nicht einmal als Kartoffeln erkennen. Für mich als Deutsche dachte ich, WIR hätten die Kartoffeln, das war ein Schock. 😉

Inkas. Ich kann Peru nicht verlassen, ohne etwas über die Inkas zu schreiben. Diese Leute machen einen so großen Eindruck auf dieses Gebiet und Land. Es dauerte nur von 1438 bis 1533 und machte immer noch einen solchen Eindruck. Bauen Sie anspruchsvolle Straßen und Wege, bauen Sie Städte und Tempel an harten Orten ohne Rad und Metallwerkzeug. Das Mauerwerk war so präzise, ​​dass viele der von ihnen gebauten Strukturen heute noch vorhanden sind, einige davon, als sie sie nach 1538 verlassen haben. Hier ein Link zu einem Video von NG über Machu Picchu und Inkas LINK. Ihre Fähigkeit, Schädeloperationen mit einer hohen Erfolgsrate durchzuführen, finde ich ziemlich unglaublich.

Wir haben es geschafft, unsere Reiselast zu verringern, indem wir viele der peruanischen Decken und das, was wir hier bekamen, zurückschickten. Ansonsten entspannen wir uns hier viel und gehen durch die Tage mit einem einfachen Zeitplan, um ein paar Dinge zu überprüfen, herumzugehen und nebenbei die Reise nach Japan zu arrangieren. Nur für zwei Tage war es eine Art Paniksituation und viel Arbeit. Wir fanden heraus, dass wir es geschafft haben, um die Goldene Woche nach Japan zu gelangen. Eine große Feiertagszeit dort. Wir fanden fast alle Unterkünfte ausgebucht und standen kurz davor, unseren Aufenthalt dort zu verkürzen. Mit Hilfe von Rebecca (Kimbos Schwester) und zwei Tagen Planungszeit scheinen wir jetzt alles zusammen zu haben. Tokio, Kyoto, Hiroshima, Miyazaki und Umgebung, dann zurück nach Osaka und Flug nach London.

An unserem letzten Abend hier hatten wir das Vergnügen, von unserem BnB-Gastgeber aus Arequipa, Roxana und seiner Familie eingeladen zu werden. Sie arbeiten in Lima, leben aber manchmal in Arequipa. Was für ein erfreuliches Erlebnis in einer multikulturellen Familie. Die peruanische Mutter, der transsilvanische Vater, die Tochter spricht fließend Deutsch, hat einen französischen Freund und der Sohn scheint sehr daran interessiert zu sein, in der internationalen Politik zu studieren und zu arbeiten. Wir hatten Sushi zusammen und es gab viele gute Gespräche und Lachen.

Roxanas Familie und wir

Lima est une immense ville d’au moins 10 millions d’habitants sur la côte du Pérou. Ce n’est pas loué pour être une beauté ou une merveille de l’Amérique du Sud, mais cela ressemble à une machine d’affaires dans la région à coup sûr. Il a une grande quantité de bord de mer, mais très peu de cela a l’air joli ou tout ce qui est utile. Nous avons fini par rester dans la région de Barranco, qui est l’une des deux régions les plus touristiques de Miraflores. D’immenses complexes d’appartements se présentent rapidement, il semble y avoir une classe moyenne distincte, nous n’avons vu que très peu de mendiants et cela semble très sûr ici. J’ai trouvé un excellent café et nous avons essayé un restaurant avec de bonnes critiques et une renommée. Je trouvais que ça ne valait pas la peine de revenir. Kjolle, nous avions réservé environ quatre semaines à l’avance et n’avions pu que nous qualifier au Bar. OK, essayons. L’accueil était devant des portes et des portes closes. L’entrée se faisait par une énorme barrière en béton, qui devait avoir 30 cm d’épaisseur de béton solide. Finalement, 5 min après notre réservation, ils ont ouvert cette porte massive à un beau jardin et à une entrée. Le bâtiment semblait avoir été construit récemment et pas grand-chose à mon goût. Il ressemblait à un intérieur encombré, à aucun style cohérent et à un peu de boîte à chaussures. Les cocktails étaient délicieux, mais je n’ai jamais aimé les plats. Tout cela semblait forcé de fantaisie et il manquait l’essentiel, le goût. Aucune sophistication nécessaire pour détecter. Juste une bonne création était ce que j’avais découvert d’un endroit comme celui-ci. Pas sucré, pas salé, juste un bon assaisonnement et une invention manquait. Nos deux plats principaux étaient juste soso, et mon dessert était juste mauvais. Pouces vers le bas.

Pérou et pommes de terre. Je ne savais pas à quel point les pommes de terre étaient centrées sur la nourriture péruvienne. Il existe plus de 330 types de pommes de terre ici. Nous en avons eu quelques uns; certains sont semblables aux types que j’avais auparavant; certains que je ne pouvais même pas reconnaître comme des pommes de terre. Pour moi, en tant qu’Allemand, je pensais que NOUS avions les pommes de terre, c’était un choc. 😉

Incas. Je ne peux pas quitter le Pérou sans écrire quelque chose sur les Incas. Ces gens font une si grande impression sur cette région et ce pays. Cela n’a duré que de 1438 à 1533, a encore eu un tel impact. Construire des rues et des chemins sophistiqués, construire des villes et des temples dans des endroits difficiles, le tout sans roue ni outils en métal. Le travail de la pierre était si précis que bon nombre des structures construites par eux sont toujours en place aujourd’hui, certaines d’entre elles exactement comme elles les ont quittées après 1538. Voici un lien vers une vidéo de NG sur le Machu Picchu et les Incas LINK. Je trouve assez incroyable leur capacité à effectuer une opération du crâne avec un taux de réussite élevé.

Nous avons réussi à alléger notre charge de voyage en renvoyant de nombreuses couvertures péruviennes et tout ce que nous avons eu ici. En dehors de cela, nous nous reposons beaucoup et passons à travers les journées avec un programme facile qui consiste à vérifier certaines choses, à marcher et à organiser votre voyage au Japon. Seulement pour deux jours, c’était une sorte de situation de panique et beaucoup de travail. Nous avons découvert que nous avions réussi à entrer au Japon autour de la Golden Week. Un grand temps de vacances public là-bas. Nous avons trouvé presque tous les logements réservés et étions sur le point de couper notre séjour là-bas à cause de cela. Avec l’aide de Rebecca (la soeur de Kimbo) et deux jours de planification, nous semblons avoir tout réuni maintenant. Tokyo, Kyoto, Hiroshima, Miyazaki et les environs, puis retour à Osaka et envol pour Londres.

Lors de notre dernière nuit ici, nous avons eu le plaisir d’être invités par notre hôte BnB d’Arequipa, Roxana et sa famille. Ils travaillent à Lima mais vivent une partie du temps à Arequipa. Quelle expérience agréable dans une famille multiculturelle. Maman péruvienne, papa transsilvanien, fille parlant couramment l’allemand, ayant un petit ami français, le fils semble très intéressé par les études et le travail en politique internationale. Nous avons eu Sushi ensemble et beaucoup de bonnes discussions et de rires.

Sleepless flight and bad food did not prevent me from getting to London on time and with my bike. I managed to build up the bike and ride (on the left side) into London to Cassandre and Gabrielle flat. They will get here tomorrow some time.

**Aug 13th at 7.15** I left Cassandre’s house in London and started my Bike trip to Nuernberg.

I used Komoot to plan the trip and to help me navigate.

Getting out of London was just as I expected. Gladly the commute traffic mostly went the other way, but the street maze was quite amazing. Every 30sec I get another direction thrown at me from the Komoot navigator. That together with left side traffic and potholes, bike lanes, cars, and pedestrians, I was working hard to crash into anyone and not run over a high curb, or run into an oncoming car. In short, my small town brain was working overtime for 2-3 hours to get through this. The 80 or so kilometers out of London are not really worth it. But I felt like riding them, just to see if my expectations are true or not. No real point to ride London Rochester. I would take the train next time (~60-80km).

Rochester seems to have a good amount of history and respective buildings. I did not stop there at all though.

The area around Canterbury is nice and the stretch from there to Dover is well worth the ride. Small roads and even Footpaths were my ways to get through there. Really charming, hilly and Rural. All Rural!! with all the smells and dirt coming with it. Where I had lunch, I had to find out that a Cup looking like a Yoghurt, a Strawberry painted on the side does not have to be a Strawberry at all. I ended up drinking Buttermilk mixed with vegetable poi as a whipping cream replacement…. Nutritious it was, not very well tasting though. I had the impression Komoot really selected great paths where it could. I got to ride total dirt roads as well as single track on the way to Dover. I was quite surprised in a positive way. The clouds gave way to drizzle, gave way to rain gave way to a downright opening of the sky just before I got to Dover. What a mess. Dover Freight terminal is not for the timid. Huge trucks and lots of them, no clear signs and no-one really knows what to do. Of course, I managed to get on the ferry, met a fellow Cyclist that did a similar route than me, he went on to ride another 120km after getting to Calais, all the way to Bruges, my destination for tomorrow. What a STUD.

At the second Hotel, I found a room for the night. France is on vacation. Will see how this plays out in the following days.

Dinner at a good Brasserie with Creme Brûlée to finish it all up. Nice.

\

\

**Aug 14th**  Getting out of Calais and on the road along the coast to Brugge. Can you spell FLAT? I had to find out that it seems like the complete coastline is built up with Hotels and resorts. I made a detour to see the coast and had to find out it was a royal waste of time. Ugly and crowded.THe roads and towns vastly improved in beauty. The cycle path mostly went along canals and if not still was a set of small lonley roads. I managed to "get a ride" with a bunch of Road riders and was propelled into a 35-40km/h with little or no extra effort. NICE. THe People of Belgium seem to be very social and communicative kind. Two or three nice interactions convinced me. Then the flats began to come my way. 1st a 2cm nail, then a glass, then something else. I made it to Brugge with a few last pump strokes, got new tire and tube and got a hotel room in spite of a bank holiday coming up.... Lucky me.

Brugge is a really nice little town, LOTS of tourists and some really nice canals and buildings. It was worth an afternoon of strolling.

Google Photos [Salkantay Trek](https://photos.app.goo.gl/GGak5oT8V1WAhQM4A) + [Machu Picchu](https://photos.app.goo.gl/o1xi54KkcFQkvVF59) # English Cusco was out next destination, it's the starting point for a lot of treks and tours. It's also at 3400m and is a welcoming town with good food (and some terrible food too) and great energy, once you forget about the mandatory diesel exhaust that seems to be present all over South America. Mumu was able to find plenty of local artisan fabric, and we found out that an overwhelming amount of fresh fruit juice will share of a cold that almost prevented both of us to go on the trek to see Machu Picchu. ### Salkantay trek It was good to see that there are so many different types of tours offered for doing the same or similar trek. What we found was that you can walk it alone, without a guide and arrange for accommodation and entry tickets by yourself or go and spend $2000 for hotel rooms and a group of guides and helpers to see the same sites. Right about that was that you seem to really get what you pay for. I have not heard of one person that did not honestly believe they were treated and got what they paid for. Good! ![](/photos/mp-salkantay-trek-5days.jpg) **Timing**: Mumu and I managed to feel symptoms of getting a cold the day before starting the trek. BUMMER. We also managed to get 3 fresh fruit and vegetable juices straight from the local San Pedro Market ladies. I could literally feel how this enabled my body to fight the cold. 1 day, 3 BIG juices and the next day we were up and running almost like new. - ![](/photos/img_20190403_102150-s.jpg) - ![](/photos/img_20190403_102801401-s.jpg) The hike went on for 5 days, 2 days with nearly 30km distance the others were a lot less. The highest point was 4620m. We could not have asked for a better weather pattern. The blue sky when it was best for the first two days, a little cloudy on the day we went down to low elevation, and it became warm, low clouds when it mystified the view and gave us the ultimate jungle experience. On the day at Machu Picchu the sky was filled with low clouds at sunrise, which were riding up to provide us with the full view once the sun was up. I could not have created a better pattern for us. A train with roof windows brought us through this really steep steep valley, and the views were nothing short of amazing. Super slow but really fun to see it all. On day 3 we were led to a woman's hut who made us coffee from her own coffee plants. Made on the wood-fired stove, in a simple drip filter, I did not expect much. But it was nothing short of amazing. She made fried plantains at the same time and thought nothing of it. Our hiking team was truly excellent. In a group of 10 tourists + 1 guide, 2 horsemen, 1 chef, and 2 assistant chefs. Our guide was a nice guy, knew some cultural stuff. His English was hard to understand and his group managing skills …… well, there was room for improvement on a few sides. He genuinely cared and tried. There was no day we did not get up before 5am on this trek. **The Trek** - ![](/photos/dsc06275-s.jpg) - ![](/photos/img_20190404_153715-s.jpg) - ![](/photos/dsc06309-s.jpg) - ![](/photos/dsc06297-s.jpg) - ![](/photos/dsc06283-s.jpg) **Then there was Machu Picchu at last.** - ![](/photos/dsc06789-s.jpg) - ![](/photos/dsc06833-s.jpg) - ![](/photos/dsc06873-s.jpg) - ![](/photos/dsc06904-s.jpg) - ![](/photos/img_20190408_162409963-s.jpg) **German** Cusco war das nächste Ziel, es ist der Ausgangspunkt für viele Wanderungen und Touren. Es ist auch auf 3400 m und ist eine einladende Stadt mit gutem Essen (und auch etwas schrecklichem Essen) und großer Energie, wenn Sie einmal den obligatorischen Dieselabgaskörper vergessen haben, der in ganz Südamerika vorhanden zu sein scheint. Mumu war in der Lage, viele einheimische Kunsthandwerkstoffe zu finden, und wir fanden heraus, dass eine überwältigende Menge an frischem Fruchtsaft an einer Erkältung beteiligt sein wird, die beinahe die Wanderung von Machu Picchu verhindert. Salkantay-Wanderung Es war schön zu sehen, dass es so viele verschiedene Arten von Touren gibt, die für die gleiche oder ähnliche Wanderung angeboten werden. Was wir gefunden haben, war, dass Sie es alleine und ohne Führer machen können und für Unterkunft und Eintrittskarten selbst sorgen können, oder 2000 Dollar für Hotelzimmer und eine Gruppe von Führern und Helfern für dieselben Sehenswürdigkeiten ausgeben. Das Richtige dabei war, dass Sie wirklich das bekommen, wofür Sie bezahlen. Ich habe nicht von einer Person gehört, die nicht ehrlich glaubte, dass sie behandelt wurden und was sie bezahlt haben. Gut! Timing: Mumu und ich hatten am Tag vor Beginn des Treks Symptome einer Erkältung. BUMMER Wir haben es auch geschafft, 3 frische Obst- und Gemüsesäfte direkt von den lokalen San Pedro Market Ladies zu erhalten. Ich konnte buchstäblich fühlen, wie dies meinem Körper ermöglichte, die Kälte zu bekämpfen. 1 Tag, 3 große Säfte und am nächsten Tag waren wir fast wie neu am Laufen. Die Wanderung dauerte 5 Tage, 2 Tage mit einer Entfernung von fast 30 km, die anderen waren viel weniger. Der höchste Punkt war 4620m. Wir hätten uns kein besseres Wettermuster wünschen können. Der blaue Himmel, als es für die ersten zwei Tage am besten war, ein wenig bewölkt an dem Tag, an dem wir auf niedrige Höhenunterschiede stiegen, und es wurde warm, tiefe Wolken, als es die Aussicht überraschte und uns das ultimative Dschungel-Erlebnis bot. An dem Tag in Machu Picchu war der Himmel bei Sonnenaufgang mit tiefen Wolken überzogen, die aufgestiegen waren, um uns die volle Sicht zu geben, sobald die Sonne aufgegangen war. Ich hätte kein besseres Muster für uns erstellen können. Ein Zug mit Dachfenstern brachte uns durch dieses wirklich steile, steile Tal, und die Aussicht war absolut erstaunlich. Super langsam, aber es macht wirklich Spaß, alles zu sehen. Am dritten Tag wurden wir zu einer Frauenhütte geführt, die uns Kaffee aus ihren eigenen Kaffeefabriken kochte. Auf dem Holzofen in einem einfachen Tropffilter hergestellt, habe ich nicht viel erwartet. Aber es war nichts weniger als erstaunlich. Sie stellte gleichzeitig gebratene Kochbananen her und dachte nichts davon. Unser Wanderteam war wirklich hervorragend. In einer Gruppe von 10 Touristen + 1 Reiseleiter, 2 Reiter, 1 Koch und 2 Küchenchefs. Unser Führer war ein netter Kerl, wusste etwas Kulturelles. Sein Englisch war schwer zu verstehen und seine Gruppe beherrschte die Fähigkeiten… Nun, auf einigen Seiten gab es Raum für Verbesserungen. Er kümmerte sich wirklich und versuchte es. Es gab keinen Tag, an dem wir auf dieser Wanderung nicht vor 5 Uhr morgens aufstanden. **French** Cusco était la prochaine destination, c’est le point de départ de nombreux treks et visites. C’est également à 3400 m d’altitude. C’est une ville accueillante, où la nourriture est bonne (et parfois très mauvaise) et où l’énergie est bonne, une fois que vous avez oublié les gaz d'échappement obligatoires qui semblent être présents partout en Amérique du Sud. Mumu a été en mesure de trouver une grande quantité de tissu artisanal local et nous avons découvert qu'une quantité écrasante de jus de fruits frais allait se partager un rhume qui nous empêchait presque tous les deux de partir en randonnée pour voir le Machu Picchu. Randonnée Salkantay C'était bon de voir qu'il y a tellement de types différents de tours proposés pour faire le même trek ou un trek similaire. Ce que nous avons constaté, c’est que vous pouvez marcher seul, sans guide et organiser votre hébergement et vos billets d’entrée par vous-même, ou aller dépenser 2 000 $ pour des chambres d’hôtel et un groupe de guides et d’aides pour visiter les mêmes sites. C’est vrai que vous semblez vraiment avoir ce pour quoi vous payez. Je n'ai pas entendu parler d'une personne qui ne croyait pas honnêtement avoir été traitée et qui avait obtenu ce pour quoi elle avait payé. Bien! Calendrier: Mumu et moi avons réussi à ressentir les symptômes d'un rhume la veille du début du trek. BUMMER. Nous avons également réussi à obtenir 3 jus de fruits et légumes frais directement des dames du marché local de San Pedro. Je pouvais littéralement sentir à quel point cela permettait à mon corps de lutter contre le froid. 1 jour, 3 gros jus et le lendemain nous étions presque comme neufs. La randonnée a duré 5 jours, 2 jours avec près de 30 km de distance, les autres étant beaucoup moins. Le point culminant était 4620m. Nous n'aurions pas pu demander une meilleure météo. Le ciel bleu quand il faisait meilleur pour les deux premiers jours, un peu nuageux le jour où nous sommes descendus à basse altitude, et il est devenu chaud, des nuages ​​bas quand il mystifiait la vue et nous a donné l'expérience ultime de jungle. Le jour de Machu Picchu, le ciel était rempli de nuages ​​bas au lever du soleil, qui montaient pour nous offrir une vue complète une fois le soleil levé. Je n'aurais pas pu créer un meilleur modèle pour nous. Un train avec des fenêtres de toit nous a fait traverser cette vallée escarpée vraiment raide, et la vue était tout simplement incroyable. Super lent mais vraiment amusant de tout voir. Le troisième jour, nous avons été conduits à une cabane de femmes qui nous a fait du café à partir de ses propres plants de café. Fabriqué sur le poêle à bois, dans un filtre goutte à goutte simple, je ne m'attendais pas à grand chose. Mais c'était tout simplement incroyable. Elle prépara des plantains frits en même temps et ne pensa pas du tout. Notre équipe de randonneurs était vraiment excellente. Dans un groupe de 10 touristes + 1 guide, 2 cavaliers, 1 chef et 2 chefs adjoints. Notre guide était un gars sympa, connaissait des trucs culturels. Son anglais était difficile à comprendre et son groupe maîtrisait les compétences… eh bien, il y avait place à amélioration de plusieurs côtés. Il s'est vraiment soucié et a essayé. Il n'y avait pas de jour nous ne nous sommes pas levés avant 5h du matin sur ce trek.
