Cusco was out next destination, it’s the starting point for a lot of treks and tours. It’s also at 3400m and is a welcoming town with good food (and some terrible food too) and great energy, once you forget about the mandatory diesel exhaust that seems to be present all over South America. Mumu was able to find plenty of local artisan fabric, and we found out that an overwhelming amount of fresh fruit juice will share of a cold that almost prevented both of us to go on the trek to see Machu Picchu.

Salkantay trek

It was good to see that there are so many different types of tours offered for doing the same or similar trek. What we found was that you can walk it alone, without a guide and arrange for accommodation and entry tickets by yourself or go and spend $2000 for hotel rooms and a group of guides and helpers to see the same sites. Right about that was that you seem to really get what you pay for. I have not heard of one person that did not honestly believe they were treated and got what they paid for. Good!

Timing: Mumu and I managed to feel symptoms of getting a cold the day before starting the trek. BUMMER. We also managed to get 3 fresh fruit and vegetable juices straight from the local San Pedro Market ladies. I could literally feel how this enabled my body to fight the cold. 1 day, 3 BIG juices and the next day we were up and running almost like new.

The hike went on for 5 days, 2 days with nearly 30km distance the others were a lot less. The highest point was 4620m. We could not have asked for a better weather pattern. The blue sky when it was best for the first two days, a little cloudy on the day we went down to low elevation, and it became warm, low clouds when it mystified the view and gave us the ultimate jungle experience. On the day at Machu Picchu the sky was filled with low clouds at sunrise, which were riding up to provide us with the full view once the sun was up. I could not have created a better pattern for us. A train with roof windows brought us through this really steep steep valley, and the views were nothing short of amazing. Super slow but really fun to see it all. On day 3 we were led to a woman’s hut who made us coffee from her own coffee plants. Made on the wood-fired stove, in a simple drip filter, I did not expect much. But it was nothing short of amazing. She made fried plantains at the same time and thought nothing of it. Our hiking team was truly excellent. In a group of 10 tourists + 1 guide, 2 horsemen, 1 chef, and 2 assistant chefs. Our guide was a nice guy, knew some cultural stuff. His English was hard to understand and his group managing skills …… well, there was room for improvement on a few sides. He genuinely cared and tried. There was no day we did not get up before 5am on this trek.

The Trek

Then there was Machu Picchu at last.

German

Cusco war das nächste Ziel, es ist der Ausgangspunkt für viele Wanderungen und Touren. Es ist auch auf 3400 m und ist eine einladende Stadt mit gutem Essen (und auch etwas schrecklichem Essen) und großer Energie, wenn Sie einmal den obligatorischen Dieselabgaskörper vergessen haben, der in ganz Südamerika vorhanden zu sein scheint. Mumu war in der Lage, viele einheimische Kunsthandwerkstoffe zu finden, und wir fanden heraus, dass eine überwältigende Menge an frischem Fruchtsaft an einer Erkältung beteiligt sein wird, die beinahe die Wanderung von Machu Picchu verhindert.

Salkantay-Wanderung
Es war schön zu sehen, dass es so viele verschiedene Arten von Touren gibt, die für die gleiche oder ähnliche Wanderung angeboten werden. Was wir gefunden haben, war, dass Sie es alleine und ohne Führer machen können und für Unterkunft und Eintrittskarten selbst sorgen können, oder 2000 Dollar für Hotelzimmer und eine Gruppe von Führern und Helfern für dieselben Sehenswürdigkeiten ausgeben. Das Richtige dabei war, dass Sie wirklich das bekommen, wofür Sie bezahlen. Ich habe nicht von einer Person gehört, die nicht ehrlich glaubte, dass sie behandelt wurden und was sie bezahlt haben. Gut!

Timing: Mumu und ich hatten am Tag vor Beginn des Treks Symptome einer Erkältung. BUMMER Wir haben es auch geschafft, 3 frische Obst- und Gemüsesäfte direkt von den lokalen San Pedro Market Ladies zu erhalten. Ich konnte buchstäblich fühlen, wie dies meinem Körper ermöglichte, die Kälte zu bekämpfen. 1 Tag, 3 große Säfte und am nächsten Tag waren wir fast wie neu am Laufen.

Die Wanderung dauerte 5 Tage, 2 Tage mit einer Entfernung von fast 30 km, die anderen waren viel weniger. Der höchste Punkt war 4620m. Wir hätten uns kein besseres Wettermuster wünschen können. Der blaue Himmel, als es für die ersten zwei Tage am besten war, ein wenig bewölkt an dem Tag, an dem wir auf niedrige Höhenunterschiede stiegen, und es wurde warm, tiefe Wolken, als es die Aussicht überraschte und uns das ultimative Dschungel-Erlebnis bot. An dem Tag in Machu Picchu war der Himmel bei Sonnenaufgang mit tiefen Wolken überzogen, die aufgestiegen waren, um uns die volle Sicht zu geben, sobald die Sonne aufgegangen war. Ich hätte kein besseres Muster für uns erstellen können. Ein Zug mit Dachfenstern brachte uns durch dieses wirklich steile, steile Tal, und die Aussicht war absolut erstaunlich. Super langsam, aber es macht wirklich Spaß, alles zu sehen. Am dritten Tag wurden wir zu einer Frauenhütte geführt, die uns Kaffee aus ihren eigenen Kaffeefabriken kochte. Auf dem Holzofen in einem einfachen Tropffilter hergestellt, habe ich nicht viel erwartet. Aber es war nichts weniger als erstaunlich. Sie stellte gleichzeitig gebratene Kochbananen her und dachte nichts davon. Unser Wanderteam war wirklich hervorragend. In einer Gruppe von 10 Touristen + 1 Reiseleiter, 2 Reiter, 1 Koch und 2 Küchenchefs. Unser Führer war ein netter Kerl, wusste etwas Kulturelles. Sein Englisch war schwer zu verstehen und seine Gruppe beherrschte die Fähigkeiten… Nun, auf einigen Seiten gab es Raum für Verbesserungen. Er kümmerte sich wirklich und versuchte es. Es gab keinen Tag, an dem wir auf dieser Wanderung nicht vor 5 Uhr morgens aufstanden.

French

Cusco était la prochaine destination, c’est le point de départ de nombreux treks et visites. C’est également à 3400 m d’altitude. C’est une ville accueillante, où la nourriture est bonne (et parfois très mauvaise) et où l’énergie est bonne, une fois que vous avez oublié les gaz d’échappement obligatoires qui semblent être présents partout en Amérique du Sud. Mumu a été en mesure de trouver une grande quantité de tissu artisanal local et nous avons découvert qu’une quantité écrasante de jus de fruits frais allait se partager un rhume qui nous empêchait presque tous les deux de partir en randonnée pour voir le Machu Picchu.

Randonnée Salkantay
C’était bon de voir qu’il y a tellement de types différents de tours proposés pour faire le même trek ou un trek similaire. Ce que nous avons constaté, c’est que vous pouvez marcher seul, sans guide et organiser votre hébergement et vos billets d’entrée par vous-même, ou aller dépenser 2 000 $ pour des chambres d’hôtel et un groupe de guides et d’aides pour visiter les mêmes sites. C’est vrai que vous semblez vraiment avoir ce pour quoi vous payez. Je n’ai pas entendu parler d’une personne qui ne croyait pas honnêtement avoir été traitée et qui avait obtenu ce pour quoi elle avait payé. Bien!

Calendrier: Mumu et moi avons réussi à ressentir les symptômes d’un rhume la veille du début du trek. BUMMER. Nous avons également réussi à obtenir 3 jus de fruits et légumes frais directement des dames du marché local de San Pedro. Je pouvais littéralement sentir à quel point cela permettait à mon corps de lutter contre le froid. 1 jour, 3 gros jus et le lendemain nous étions presque comme neufs.

La randonnée a duré 5 jours, 2 jours avec près de 30 km de distance, les autres étant beaucoup moins. Le point culminant était 4620m. Nous n’aurions pas pu demander une meilleure météo. Le ciel bleu quand il faisait meilleur pour les deux premiers jours, un peu nuageux le jour où nous sommes descendus à basse altitude, et il est devenu chaud, des nuages ​​bas quand il mystifiait la vue et nous a donné l’expérience ultime de jungle. Le jour de Machu Picchu, le ciel était rempli de nuages ​​bas au lever du soleil, qui montaient pour nous offrir une vue complète une fois le soleil levé. Je n’aurais pas pu créer un meilleur modèle pour nous. Un train avec des fenêtres de toit nous a fait traverser cette vallée escarpée vraiment raide, et la vue était tout simplement incroyable. Super lent mais vraiment amusant de tout voir. Le troisième jour, nous avons été conduits à une cabane de femmes qui nous a fait du café à partir de ses propres plants de café. Fabriqué sur le poêle à bois, dans un filtre goutte à goutte simple, je ne m’attendais pas à grand chose. Mais c’était tout simplement incroyable. Elle prépara des plantains frits en même temps et ne pensa pas du tout. Notre équipe de randonneurs était vraiment excellente. Dans un groupe de 10 touristes + 1 guide, 2 cavaliers, 1 chef et 2 chefs adjoints. Notre guide était un gars sympa, connaissait des trucs culturels. Son anglais était difficile à comprendre et son groupe maîtrisait les compétences… eh bien, il y avait place à amélioration de plusieurs côtés. Il s’est vraiment soucié et a essayé. Il n’y avait pas de jour nous ne nous sommes pas levés avant 5h du matin sur ce trek.
MC Cains funeral and some outstanding speeches, but predictably no action

[https://nyti.ms/2MIOESg](https://nyti.ms/2MIOESg)

They sat in seats of honor, near the front of Washington National Cathedral. They bowed their heads when appropriate. They looked up pensively and listened.

By all appearances, they were honoring their departed colleague, Senator John Sidney McCain III, during [a majestic ceremony on Saturday](https://www.nytimes.com/2018/09/01/us/politics/john-mccain-funeral.html). And by doing so they were showing America that leaders of both parties reject the hateful, petty, law-defying politics of President Trump. They were showing America what a better nation could look like.

But it was all an act — a cynical, hypocritical act that McCain, who had a keen eye for hypocrisy, would have seen right through.

It was an act for Mitch McConnell, the Senate majority leader. It was an act for Paul Ryan, the speaker of the House. It was an act, most jarringly, for Lindsey Graham, McCain’s dear friend and the senior senator from South Carolina. It was an act for Orrin Hatch, Rob Portman and nearly all of the other Republican members of Congress who attended the service.

It was an act because they have not kept faith with the principles that McCain held dear — and [that he himself organized](https://www.nytimes.com/2018/08/29/us/politics/mccain-funeral-trump.html) his memorial service to celebrate, as a clear rebuke to Trump and Trumpism. McConnell, Ryan, Graham and the others have instead done the very opposite of keeping faith. They have made possible Trump’s hateful, petty, law-defying politics.

Despite running a branch of government that the Constitution makes equal to the presidency, they have meekly assented to Trump. Entrusted with power, they have chosen complicity.

They have refused to defend America’s national security in the face of [Russian attacks](https://www.nytimes.com/2018/07/16/opinion/trump-and-putin-vs-america.html). They have refused to defend [the rule of law](https://www.nytimes.com/2017/06/06/opinion/the-lawless-presidency.html) against Trump’s attacks. They have refused to defend the F.B.I., [the Justice Department](https://www.nytimes.com/2018/04/29/opinion/the-sense-of-justice-that-were-losing.html) and the First Amendment. They have refused to defend the basic civil rights that Trump seeks to deny to dark-skinned American citizens, including [the right to vote](https://www.nytimes.com/2018/06/19/opinion/a-crusader-against-voter-fraud-fails-to-prove-his-case.html) and [the right to hold a passport](https://www.nytimes.com/2018/08/31/opinion/trump-birtherism-citizenship-texas.html).

When George W. Bush said the following words in [his eulogy](https://www.nytimes.com/2018/09/01/us/politics/george-w-bush-john-mccain-eulogy.html) for McCain, what did the congressional Republicans in attendance think that Bush possibly could have meant:

“He was honorable, always recognizing that his opponents were still patriots and human beings. He loved freedom, with the passion of a man who knew its absence. He respected the dignity inherent in every life, a dignity that does not stop at borders and cannot be erased by dictators. Perhaps above all, John detested the abuse of power. He could not abide bigots and swaggering despots.”

When [Barack Obama’s eulogy](https://www.nytimes.com/2018/09/01/us/politics/barack-obama-john-mccain-funeral-eulogy.html) was organized around a recitation of McCain’s principles, what contrast could Obama have possibly been drawing:

“John cared about the institutions of self-government — our Constitution, our Bill of Rights, rule of law and separation of powers. … He understood that if we get in the habit of bending the truth to suit political expediency or party orthodoxy, our democracy will not work. … John understood, as J.F.K. understood, as Ronald Reagan understood, that part of what makes our country great is that our membership is based not on our bloodline; not on what we look like, what our last names are.”

And when Meghan McCain rose and did what her father advised for this occasion — she showed them how tough she was — surely the congressional Republicans knew exactly [what she was referring to](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/read-full-text-meghan-mccain-s-speech-john-mccain-s-n905746):

“The America of John McCain is generous and welcoming and bold. She is resourceful and confident and secure. She meets her responsibilities. She speaks quietly because she is strong. America does not boast because she has no need to. The America of John McCain has no need to be made great again because America was always great.”

The cathedral then broke into applause, not exactly a common occurrence during a eulogy.

Over the last few years, McCain sometimes struggled with how to respond to Trump. McCain first refused to endorse Trump, then caved, unfortunately, before [ultimately revoking](https://www.nytimes.com/2016/10/23/opinion/sunday/john-mccains-choice-on-trump.html) the endorsement. Once Trump took office, McCain [went further](https://www.nytimes.com/2017/09/19/opinion/mccain-healthcare-graham-cassidy.html) in trying to restrain him than nearly any other Republican — but [not as far](https://projects.fivethirtyeight.com/congress-trump-score/john-mccain/) as he could have. So McCain understood the political tensions facing the congressional Republicans he leaves behind: Trump remains extremely popular with Republican voters, and he can also help conservatives achieve their policy goals.

In the end, however, McCain saw the situation clearly. Political expediency and short-term policy goals are not worth undermining basic American values. It’s not even close.

In his final book, McCain described Trump’s behavior as “disturbing” and “appalling.” In one of McCain’s [final public statements](https://twitter.com/SenJohnMcCain/status/1018919182904299520?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Etweetembed%7Ctwterm%5E1018919182904299520&ref_url=http%3A%2F%2Ftime.com%2F5339932%2Fjohn-mccain-statement-trump-putin-meeting%2Fwww.bostonglobe.com/news/politics/2018/07/16/read-john-mccain-statement-trump-meeting-with-putin/U88mUGY32Yilx3F4OlibNM/amp.html), he called out Trump’s “naïveté, egotism, false equivalence, and sympathy for autocrats.” And in McCain’s final public act, he turned his memorial service into a piercing alarm about a president of the United States damaging and threatening his own country.

The congressional Republicans inside the Washington National Cathedral on Saturday would surely say they came to honor John McCain. But they were there for show. Faced with a choice, they have rejected McCain’s America for Trump’s.

Meeting Jade Jagger in Oaxaca - can you believe it

English

Google [photos](https://photos.app.goo.gl/vDv4H1ycEorN66Bt8)

**Jade Jagger** ([Daughter](https://www.google.com/imgres?imgurl=https%3A%2F%2Fta-images.condecdn.net%2Fimage%2FxrVqoQkMpdj%2Fcrop%2F405%2Ff%2FJade-Jagger-and-Mick-Jagger-Tatler-10dec14_pr_b.jpg&imgrefurl=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tatler.com%2Fgallery%2Ftara-bernerd-and-jade-jaggers-christmas-party&docid=4051LJKxgIWFVM&tbnid=waEobssVeSZa_M%3A&vet=1&w=405&h=607&hl=en-US&source=sh%2Fx%2Fim) of Mick Jagger): We actually did! We saw her and her son and her husband. I, of course, had no idea, but Mumu did of course.

When I heard about Oaxaca the 1st times, I hardly knew how to pronounce it. Now, I grew to be a pretty big fan of the place. There is so much more to this town than great black or brown MOLE on your plate. What an upbeat, interesting and livable town it is. When you dive in, there all of a sudden are neighborhoods that seem to connect people and they thrive with little town marketplaces that support most everything from Fruit and Veggie vendors to sellers of all different kinds of food, then some good quality clothing and baskets and the whole hood seems to go there to spend their weekend morning with each other. Some areas are more touristy though and still very easy to digest. Then there are plenty of interesting places to visit near the town in just a 1/2h to 1h trips in what they call “colectivos” here. Taxi cars, that only travel from A to B when enough people are in the car and share the cost of the ride. The public transport system in Mexico is truly amazing. I don’t think there are many places you can’t get with public transport.

People we met here:

My “Support local Bees” T-shirt from Danielle and Toro proved again to be a people catcher. Right on the 1st day in town, we met this Group of people in ...… Who knows where we met. We quickly came to find out we are all Beekeepers. We ended up meeting Ed and Ken again and again for lunch and dinner where we got a hit list of more Oaxacan places to go and enjoy good company in the process. What a treat to meet them, what a treat to have brought this T-Shirt. Thanks, Danielle!! We met Ainka, Victor and Ilene. It was fun and social. The Mezcal did help in this process for sure. We, of course, went to **_Monte Alban_** which is another historic place where Aztec Pyramid ruins and other ceremonial places are to see. It is somewhat smaller than Teotihuacan near Mexico City but it seemed more inviting and fewer tourist for sure.

![](/photos/mtalban-s.jpg)

The calcium formed pools of **_Herve el Aqua_** are truly impressive and worth a visit. The fact that we visitors are allowed to not only touch them but swim in it is great, but at the same time disturbing as each of the visitors will leave a clear mark on the place and prevent the calcium from forming in the future. Mumu and I went for an 18km hike on the way back from there which was really hot but felt great to stretch those legs. It was also the 1st time I managed to startle a local woman, just by walking down her street while she came out of the house. I guess she really was not used to Gringos there.

- ![](/photos/hierve-pool-s.jpg)
    
- ![](/photos/hierve-fall-s.jpg)
    
- ![](/photos/hierve-puddle-s.jpg)
    

**Oaxaca** now is for me a real place to come back to and stay for more than just a few days. It seems to me to be so welcoming that I could see us staying here for a few months to escape the cold winters somewhere else.

**Places we liked**

**Food**: 

- **La Popular**; our go-to place for every time and every day
- **Itanony**; A true Mexican neighborhood place
- **Casa Oaxaca**; it’s a pretty swanky place, can seem a little ritzy but they do offer a good menu and a pretty upscale environment
- **Los Danzantes**; if you want to eat in a well-designed restaurant and have really good food!, and don’t mind eating next to square-shaped crushed cars
- **La Olla**; was supposed to be great but we found it just ok
- **Cooking school**, there are so many and while Gerardo and his family did a really great job for us, I am sure other experiences are just as great

**Coffee**: 

- **Cafebre:** hands down the best coffee in town no doubt, 
- **Boulenc:** with probably the best bread and pastry offering in town and great coffee too. 

**Drinks:**

- **Mezcaloteca** was where we got our education on Mezcal, not only theoretical but got to try a few of them as well. We found it to be a great way to know more about this way under appreciated drink (at least it was for me) Almost only Agave for Mezcal, only blue Agave for Tequilla. 
- **Nanixhe** was a pace we wanted to get to but did not manage. 

**Things to do and see:**

- St Augustine Art Center
- Botanical Garden right next to Santo Domingo Church
- Really great Ceramic in Atzompa
- Herve del Aqua the calcium formed pools
- Monte Alban
- Cactus Garden from Heaven - Vives Verdes

- ![](/photos/cactus-forrest-s.jpg)
    
- ![](/photos/agave-s.jpg)
    

After a seemingly endless overnight bus trip to San Cristobal, we are finally here. Because of a road closure, we took a long detour and had 15 instead of 11 hours on the bus. VERY comfortable and safe driver, just a long time on the bus.

Google [photos](https://photos.app.goo.gl/vDv4H1ycEorN66Bt8)

**Jade Jagger** ([fille](https://www.google.com/imgres?imgurl=https%3A%2F%2Fta-images.condecdn.net%2Fimage%2FxrVqoQkMpdj%2Fcrop%2F405%2Ff%2FJade-Jagger-and-Mick-Jagger-Tatler-10dec14_pr_b.jpg&imgrefurl=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tatler.com%2Fgallery%2Ftara-bernerd-and-jade-jaggers-christmas-party&docid=4051LJKxgIWFVM&tbnid=waEobssVeSZa_M%3A&vet=1&w=405&h=607&hl=en-US&source=sh%2Fx%2Fim) de Mick Jagger): C'est ce que nous avons fait! Nous l'avons vue avec son fils et son mari. Bien entendu, je n'en savais rien, mais Mumu, bien sûr.

Quand j'ai entendu parler d'Oaxaca les 1ères fois, je ne savais presque pas comment le prononcer. Maintenant, je suis devenu un très grand fan de l'endroit. Il y a tellement plus dans cette ville que de grands mules noires ou brunes dans votre assiette. Quelle ville optimiste, intéressante et agréable à vivre. Lorsque vous plongez, il y a tout à coup des quartiers qui semblent connecter les gens et ils s'épanouissent avec les petits marchés de la ville qui supportent presque tout, des vendeurs de fruits et légumes aux vendeurs de toutes sortes d'aliments, puis des vêtements toute la hotte semble y aller pour passer leur fin de semaine matinale les uns avec les autres. Certaines zones sont plus touristiques et très faciles à digérer. Ensuite, il existe de nombreux endroits intéressants à visiter près de la ville en seulement 1 / 2h à 1h dans ce qu’on appelle des «colectivos». Les taxis, qui voyagent de A à B seulement quand il y a suffisamment de monde dans la voiture et partagent le coût de la course. Le système de transport en commun au Mexique est vraiment incroyable. Je ne pense pas qu’il y ait beaucoup d’endroits que vous ne pouvez pas utiliser avec les transports en commun.

Personnes rencontrées ici:

Mon t-shirt “Support local Bees” de Danielle et Toro a de nouveau attiré les regards. Dès le premier jour en ville, nous avons rencontré ce groupe de personnes à …… Qui sait où nous nous sommes rencontrés. Nous avons rapidement découvert que nous sommes tous des apiculteurs. Nous avons fini par rencontrer Ed et Ken encore et encore pour le déjeuner et le dîner, où nous avons reçu une liste de lieux à visiter qui comptent d’autres endroits à Oaxaca où il fait bon vivre et être en bonne compagnie. Quel plaisir de les rencontrer, quel plaisir d'avoir apporté ce t-shirt. Merci Danielle !! Nous avons rencontré Ainka, Victor et Ilene. C'était amusant et social. Le Mezcal a bien aidé dans ce processus. Nous sommes bien sûr allés à Monte Alban, un autre lieu historique où les ruines de la pyramide aztèque et d’autres lieux de cérémonie sont à voir. Il est un peu plus petit que Teotihuacan près de Mexico mais il semblait plus invitant et moins touristique.

Als ich das erste Mal von Oaxaca hörte, wusste ich kaum, wie man es ausspricht. Nun wurde ich ein ziemlich großer Fan des Ortes. Es gibt so viel mehr in dieser Stadt als ein tolles schwarzes oder braunes MOLE auf Ihrem Teller. Was für eine fröhliche, interessante und lebenswerte Stadt. Wenn Sie eintauchen, gibt es plötzlich Nachbarschaften, die Menschen zu verbinden scheinen, und sie gedeihen mit kleinen Marktplätzen auf dem Markt, die fast alles unterstützen, von Obst- und Gemüseverkäufern bis hin zu Verkäufern aller Arten von Lebensmitteln die ganze Haube scheint dorthin zu gehen, um ihr Wochenende morgens miteinander zu verbringen. Einige Gegenden sind jedoch eher touristisch und dennoch sehr leicht zu verdauen. Es gibt viele interessante Orte in der Nähe der Stadt, die in nur 1 / 2h bis 1h Fahrt zu besuchen sind, was sie hier "colectivos" nennen. Der Mezcal hat dabei sicherlich geholfen. Wir sind natürlich zum Monte Alban gefahren, einem anderen historischen Ort, wo die Ruinen der Aztekenpyramide und andere zeremonielle Orte zu sehen sind. Es ist etwas kleiner als Teotihuacan in der Nähe von Mexiko-Stadt, schien aber einladender und weniger touristisch zu sein.

Die von Kalzium gebildeten Pools von Herve el Aqua sind wirklich beeindruckend und einen Besuch wert. Jade Jagger (Daughter of Mick Jagger): We actually did! We saw her and her son and her husband. I, of course, had no idea, but Mumu did of course.

When I heard about Oaxaca the 1st times, I hardly knew how to pronounce it. Now, I grew to be a pretty big fan of the place. There is so much more to this town than great black or brown MOLE on your plate. What an upbeat, interesting and livable town it is. When you dive in, there all of a sudden are neighborhoods that seem to connect people and they thrive with little town marketplaces that support most everything from Fruit and Veggie vendors to sellers of all different kinds of food, then some good quality clothing and baskets and the whole hood seems to go there to spend their weekend morning with each other. Some areas are more touristy though and still very easy to digest. Then there are plenty of interesting places to visit near the town in just a 1/2h to 1h trips in what they call “colectivos” here. Taxi cars, that only travel from A to B when enough people are in the car and share the cost of the ride. The public transport system in Mexico is truly amazing. I don’t think there are many places you can’t get with public transport.

People we met here:

My “Support local Bees” T-shirt from Danielle and Toro proved again to be a people catcher. Right on the 1st day in town, we met this Group of people in …… Who knows where we met. We quickly came to find out we are all Beekeepers. We ended up meeting Ed and Ken again and again for lunch and dinner where we got a hit list of more Oaxacan places to go and enjoy good company in the process. What a treat to meet them, what a treat to have brought this T-Shirt. Thanks, Danielle!! We met Ainka, Victor and Ilene. It was fun and social. The Mezcal did help in this process for sure. We, of course, went to Monte Alban which is another historic place where Aztec Pyramid ruins and other ceremonial places are to see. It is somewhat smaller than Teotihuacan near Mexico City but it seemed more inviting and fewer tourist for sure.

The calcium formed pools of Herve el Aqua are truly impressive and worth a visit. The fact that we visitors are allowed to not only touch them but swim in it is great, but at the same time disturbing as each of the visitors will leave a clear mark on the place and prevent the calcium from forming in the future. Mumu and I went for an 18km hike on the way back from there which was really hot but felt great to stretch those legs. It was also the 1st time I managed to startle a local woman, just by walking down her street while she came out of the house. I guess she really was not used to Gringos there.

Oaxaca now is for me a real place to come back to and stay for more than just a few days. It seems to me to be so welcoming that I could see us staying here for a few months to escape the cold winters somewhere else.

Places we liked

Food: 

  • La Popular; our go-to place for every time and every day
  • Itanony; A true Mexican neighborhood place
  • Casa Oaxaca; it’s a pretty swanky place, can seem a little ritzy but they do offer a good menu and a pretty upscale environment
  • Los Danzantes; if you want to eat in a well-designed restaurant and have really good food!, and don’t mind eating next to square-shaped crushed cars
  • La Olla; was supposed to be great but we found it just ok
  • Cooking school, there are so many and while Gerardo and his family did a really great job for us, I am sure other experiences are just as great

Coffee: 

  • Cafebre: hands down the best coffee in town no doubt, 
  • Boulenc: with probably the best bread and pastry offering in town and great coffee too. 

Drinks:

  • Mezcaloteca was where we got our education on Mezcal, not only theoretical but got to try a few of them as well. We found it to be a great way to know more about this way under appreciated drink (at least it was for me) Almost only Agave for Mezcal, only blue Agave for Tequilla. 
  • Nanixhe was a pace we wanted to get to but did not manage. 

Things to do and see:

  • St Augustine Art Center

  • Botanical Garden right next to Santo Domingo Church

  • Really great Ceramic in Atzompa

  • Herve del Aqua the calcium formed pools

  • Monte Alban

  • Cactus Garden from Heaven - Vives Verdes

Moving into Macia - May 4th to October 2nd - Motivated and Focussed

Google pictures [LINK](https://photos.app.goo.gl/Fvtj6fDHpEmmSPrp7)

It's been 2 months since the last update on the house and us in Tuscany. It was hard and focussed, it was taxing and then some more. But finally we moved in. YES, we can barely believe it ourself. October 2nd was the first night we spent in the house. It is not finished, but it is livable. We have hot water, we have a pellet heater for the kitchen / living room, we have floor covering in all rooms, we have all bathrooms operational (but shower cabins are strangely absent). We also had a few doors in the house at the time, now we have them all. I can't tell you how good it feels to sleep in your own bed, to eat and prepare food in a kitchen that is not tiny and have a fridge that is big enough so you can actually store stuff in. Going though your day knowing this is not your home. It's stable, will not change, and you have influence in what get's done. The word **HOME** certainly filled with new and important meaning for us two. It is really incredible the amount of tasks there are to make a home. I am also eternally grateful to the construction team for pulling off the project to schedule. In a house of this age, there are so many unknowns and so many surprises to deal with. Still the initial schedule of 3 1/2 months was held, and we moved in. YEPEEEEEE

In August Muriel decided it would be the best for her to eject herself from the project and visit family in Paris for a month. Just before that, Cassandre and Gabriele came to visit us, which was a huge treat!!. Then, to top it off, Sabrina and her boyfriend Leonardo came see us just before she left. Then, I had a little more time for myself as it is traditionally the month where Italians go on vacation. Though COVID sent everyone in a shut down in the Spring and start of the summer, but Italians cannot and will not miss out of their summer beach time. With or without COVID. I managed to build a Tuscan stone wall with Claudio, the lead builder on the project. He really built it and I was more a helper. But I learned a lot and was not only useless. It will frame the area of the future wooden hot tub. It took 4 a little more than 1/2 days to build it. The heat was just too intense to continue past 13.00 or 14.00. I am so so proud of the fact that I was part of it.

![](/photos/wall-s.jpg)

![](/photos/img_20200617_103831-s.jpg)

August also started the time of harvest. I made a lot of Blackberry jam, all straight from the property. Interestingly they looked a little dull and small during the hot and dry times of August. They tasted intense though. After a good Tuscan rain, they looked shiny, plump and glorious. So I went out for another picking session. The result was a little more diluted taste. Still good, but less intense. They were cooked and made to glorious jam anyway. Then there were yellow plums, purple plums, pears..... So good, so rich. It felt rushed to squeeze in jam making sessions after a full day of work at the house, but it also felt good to do something for the next year, plan ahead and be certain it will actually happen for a change. Later in September, we got to harvest Hazelnuts and walnuts. So many, I had to give up for this year to try and harvest them all.

![](/photos/dsc05823-s.jpg)

I also started building the kitchen at the start of September. It is not an easy task and I had more trouble making progress just because every day would start with a talk with the workers, asking questions, answering and making decisions, and and and. Then after lunch I would have an hour or two to work on that kitchen only to be more interrupted by questions. Only once all the workers left the site was I able to start some focussed kitchen work. Everything had to be super stable and even as the Marble countertop will be very heavy on the cabinets and would not tolerate any wiggling of give. Uneven floors and walls and all the rest of it did not help make this easy. but now, now I am finally done with it and wait for the delivery of the Marble. It is ready since Friday, I plan to pick it up and install next week. In the mean time we have OSB boards as countertops.

![](/photos/pxl_20200929_112803496-s.jpg)

Outdoors on the property we made huge progress through hiring a farmer and two of his big machines. a big tractor with a mowing device that seems indestructible to me, and an excavator with an even more rugged weed/bush/tree eater as attachment. Two people were working for 4 days, 10 hours a day. Now the property tot he hill side is no longer recognizable. It is like night and day. The terrace walls are visible, the blackberry bushes are gone (for now) and we can actually see what we have. It used to be like a jungle.

![](/photos/img_20200916_141040.jpg)

We are so overworked and so tired and still now and finally so happy. We can really not understand what happened the last months. We finally have a home.

Don't get me wrong, there is so much more to do and to work on and to build and to figure out and and and. This project will go on till at least January. But we have a home.

Just about a week ago, Manu and Marine came to visit and were the 1st to actually leep with us at the house. They brought small but BIG precents with them. Two young kittens they had rescued ~1month before in France, now relocated them to Italy to stay with us. SUPER TREAT.

![](/photos/pxl_20201011_175558941-s.jpg)

Google pictures LINK

It’s been 2 months since the last update on the house and us in Tuscany. It was hard and focussed, it was taxing and then some more. But finally we moved in. YES, we can barely believe it ourself. October 2nd was the first night we spent in the house. It is not finished, but it is livable. We have hot water, we have a pellet heater for the kitchen / living room, we have floor covering in all rooms, we have all bathrooms operational (but shower cabins are strangely absent). We also had a few doors in the house at the time, now we have them all. I can’t tell you how good it feels to sleep in your own bed, to eat and prepare food in a kitchen that is not tiny and have a fridge that is big enough so you can actually store stuff in. Going though your day knowing this is not your home. It’s stable, will not change, and you have influence in what get’s done. The word HOME certainly filled with new and important meaning for us two. It is really incredible the amount of tasks there are to make a home. I am also eternally grateful to the construction team for pulling off the project to schedule. In a house of this age, there are so many unknowns and so many surprises to deal with. Still the initial schedule of 3 1/2 months was held, and we moved in. YEPEEEEEE

In August Muriel decided it would be the best for her to eject herself from the project and visit family in Paris for a month. Just before that, Cassandre and Gabriele came to visit us, which was a huge treat!!. Then, to top it off, Sabrina and her boyfriend Leonardo came see us just before she left. Then, I had a little more time for myself as it is traditionally the month where Italians go on vacation. Though COVID sent everyone in a shut down in the Spring and start of the summer, but Italians cannot and will not miss out of their summer beach time. With or without COVID. I managed to build a Tuscan stone wall with Claudio, the lead builder on the project. He really built it and I was more a helper. But I learned a lot and was not only useless. It will frame the area of the future wooden hot tub. It took 4 a little more than 1/2 days to build it. The heat was just too intense to continue past 13.00 or 14.00. I am so so proud of the fact that I was part of it.

August also started the time of harvest. I made a lot of Blackberry jam, all straight from the property. Interestingly they looked a little dull and small during the hot and dry times of August. They tasted intense though. After a good Tuscan rain, they looked shiny, plump and glorious. So I went out for another picking session. The result was a little more diluted taste. Still good, but less intense. They were cooked and made to glorious jam anyway. Then there were yellow plums, purple plums, pears… So good, so rich. It felt rushed to squeeze in jam making sessions after a full day of work at the house, but it also felt good to do something for the next year, plan ahead and be certain it will actually happen for a change. Later in September, we got to harvest Hazelnuts and walnuts. So many, I had to give up for this year to try and harvest them all.

I also started building the kitchen at the start of September. It is not an easy task and I had more trouble making progress just because every day would start with a talk with the workers, asking questions, answering and making decisions, and and and. Then after lunch I would have an hour or two to work on that kitchen only to be more interrupted by questions. Only once all the workers left the site was I able to start some focussed kitchen work. Everything had to be super stable and even as the Marble countertop will be very heavy on the cabinets and would not tolerate any wiggling of give. Uneven floors and walls and all the rest of it did not help make this easy. but now, now I am finally done with it and wait for the delivery of the Marble. It is ready since Friday, I plan to pick it up and install next week. In the mean time we have OSB boards as countertops.

Outdoors on the property we made huge progress through hiring a farmer and two of his big machines. a big tractor with a mowing device that seems indestructible to me, and an excavator with an even more rugged weed/bush/tree eater as attachment. Two people were working for 4 days, 10 hours a day. Now the property tot he hill side is no longer recognizable. It is like night and day. The terrace walls are visible, the blackberry bushes are gone (for now) and we can actually see what we have. It used to be like a jungle.

We are so overworked and so tired and still now and finally so happy. We can really not understand what happened the last months. We finally have a home.

Don’t get me wrong, there is so much more to do and to work on and to build and to figure out and and and. This project will go on till at least January. But we have a home.

Mumu and I finally made it to my home town Nuernberg. Being able to see my Mom for a while was way way overdue and the rest of the family crowd in similar ways.

My Mom's place is always stylish, beyond clean and she is as welcoming as you can possibly want it. ==> Son and Mumu are very well taken care off. In all and anyways. 1st and 2nd there is always food. You all need to understand one concept my Grandmom seems to have implanted in all family members. If you have guests and ask if they want food, more food or anything in this arena ==> you don't really want to give. You need to buy it, prepare it and load it on their plate, no question asked. Only if they violently refuse and make their point several times that no more food fits in, then. And only then are you allowed to back off and stop cooking. I am overdoing this of course, but you get the idea.

### Reunion with my Rock-Lobster

After almost one full year of separation from my bicycle, I found her again and I found her in good condition, no hard feelings and a great reunion. Just a little air and a few drops of oil on the chain. She was good for a spin in the Pegniz valley and then we two went "all the way". The Frankenjura is just north of Nuernberg and holds a wealth of streets and trails that all are calling me, all the time. "RIDE ME" come and ride me, I missed you for 25 years. It took some time to become familiar with the area again, but a few times I could confidently disagree with Google Maps and found known territory. Getting lost when I was wrong seemed also part of the game of getting back together.

\

### The Alps with the extended Nerb family and more new/old friends

Christian and Michael seem to have gone up to the Buchsteinhuette for as long as they can remember. Now they belong to the club that owns these two huts. One is run by a "Wirt" and the other is there for the club members and their guests. Just bring your food and you are good for a weekend. Or don't and eat at the "Wirt" and worry about even less. It's a very comfortable and sizable hut, giving room for about 40 people. Electricity is provided by their own water power turbine, backup is a diesel generator. The heat comes from local wood, fun to be supplied by yourself. This is not your Sierra type setup, my friends. Alms on almost every path you might desire to hike, one after every 45min or so. This is incredible. They provide you food at 1600m elevation and it tastes good, does not cost the world and comes with an amazing view, a friendly smile and advise for anyone who feels the need for it. We bought some local honey, were a little early for local cheese but managed to get raw milk and Buttermilk. And it tasted, ... you guessed it. It tasted like cow and actual milk. Amazing. Michael did an amazing job setting up the place, getting us all organized, setting up the Bondfire, BBQ, and and and so much more. This man is on fire. Thanks again, Michael. TO say meeting Chisstian again is an understatement. Thanks for inviting us to this yearly ritual of your team.

Mumu and I finally made it to my home town Nuernberg. Being able to see my Mom for a while was way way overdue and the rest of the family crowd in similar ways.

My Mom’s place is always stylish, beyond clean and she is as welcoming as you can possibly want it. ==> Son and Mumu are very well taken care off. In all and anyways. 1st and 2nd there is always food. You all need to understand one concept my Grandmom seems to have implanted in all family members. If you have guests and ask if they want food, more food or anything in this arena ==> you don’t really want to give. You need to buy it, prepare it and load it on their plate, no question asked. Only if they violently refuse and make their point several times that no more food fits in, then. And only then are you allowed to back off and stop cooking. I am overdoing this of course, but you get the idea.

The Frankenjura is just north of Nuernberg and holds a wealth of streets and trails that all are calling me, all the time. “RIDE ME” come and ride me, I missed you for 25 years. Out of Sicily, travel to Poppi and 2 weeks in the Casentino Valley

Google Photos [LINK](https://photos.app.goo.gl/XvrWiAtQ6Lfqy2wa8)

We sent 2 days in Palermo. A city I expected to be chaotic and ridden with Mafia BS. None of this was true for us. Don't get me wrong, it did not become our favorite city all in one day, NO!! But Palermo presented itself to us quite pleasantly. We continued to have good food, coffee, and dessert, I got a good bike ride in, Mumu finally found her Puppets. And all that without being mugged or even feeling it would happen. Not bad, I would say.

We took the night Ferry to Naples, and there we were received by a city we found hard to like. The TAXI overcharged us and most of the streets we walked seemed somehow strange. I never felt as insecure anywhere in Italy as I felt here in only the 5 hours we spent there. The Pizza was good, and I really have no reason to go back there. But I do know I would go back with someone who knows this place really well.

On the train, we went and off to Florence in only 2.5 hours. We are now hunkering down in Poppi, in a house we rented for the 6 weeks we stay. We thought we will need to sign some house papers on Nov 12 (11/12 or was it 12/11) I just found out the hard way the signature will only happen on Dec 11. We will spend one extra month in Europe but we will go to London for a Family ThanksGiving then figure out what to do and where to go till we can sign this paper finally.

HOUSE: We finally have the impression we will get the house. We will get it late (May 2020) but we think we will. That is kind of a shock for us. Good shock, but still a shock. We found out we can get great tasting Mushrooms straight from our yeard.

\

I found a riding buddy for 3 weeks, Dave from Melbourne Australia. To kick things off we rode a quick trip to Talla and back. I think I should have been charged the Inter City Express fare. This man knows how to ride, and ride fast. I gave it all I had and we been on the road for 1.5 hours, did more than 40km and a bunch of climbing. My steely friend and I have not been on the move like this in a while. Dave could have left me in the dust still, but I was happy with the ride and with the fact I had a riding buddy.

Now, I am **WORKING** again. Yes, I am working. My 1st day today. I am helping out a very well known Blacksmith of the Valley as he has a crunch time and can use a hand. It was hard for me to stand in a shop for 8+ hours and doing physical labor as well as problem-solving with him. It was fun and will be fun tomorrow, but it was hard. Maybe I can get him to teach me a couple of skills when crunch time is over. I would love that, but let's see.

\

It is now 3 weeks since we are allowed to interact with the people around us now. Italians that is now. In case this is news to you; there is a lot of passion in Italian culture. Passion for life, for food, for friends, for a sport that you watch, for the sport that you do, for the color you pick for your new sweater, for the type of car you choose, for the wine you drink, for for for … for most anything these beautiful people see and touch.

I found it hard to stay in Quarantine with Muriel. I think anyone understands 14 days stuck without much of any interaction with others is hard. I love my Main Squeeze and then there is still the need to interact with others. I just remember this scenario. We stay for 14 days in this house, we get food bought and delivered by our awesome Landlords Stefano and Patricia, with their kids Marco and Lisa and their friends Medi and Bateman. I could not be anything else but overwhelmed by the kindness but more the thirst for life of these people. We barely met and they started giving and talking and including us. It was an instant family, really. The absolutely stunning scenery we are staying in seemed to grow a little stale on us, with only the two of us around each other. It was still amazing and great, but the secret sauce was somehow missing. The question arose in me, why did we actually choose Italy, why Tuscany, why Casentino Valley? What the hell are we doing here and why did we even get started with all this? These questions piled up in a hurry during this quiet time of Quarantine. As soon as our hosts arrived in their house, right next to ours, these questions received answers quickly. The secret sauce, what we like so much about Italy and the area of the Casentino Valley, the “sauce” is simply the people and their passion. A passion for life a spark that is infectious. As soon as they joined us, close to our house, these questions evaporated into two smiles and a little lift of the heart. THANK YOU.

\

We are now 2+ weeks into this ownership. We are so thrilled and we are working hard to get the place ready for the construction work this Monday. The house was almost completely full of old furniture and crap, the basement rooms were filled with Farming tools and stuff that I still cannot believe one man can collect in a lifetime. Selecting anything that would be useful for us, neat to keep, and finding ways to get rid of the rest was the task for 2 weeks. With the help of Medhi, Marco, and Silvio for the house, Francesco for the Grass we managed to make this place almost livable during this time. Only to now let in contractors to demolish walls, tear down tiles, and re-install all the things we actually want and need, bringing the heating, water, and electrical systems into the 21st century. Our expectation is that in 3 1/2 months, this will all be over and we can move in. During this time we also managed to move the furniture we brought over from California into the 2nd house. The movers were an excellent example of what I start to expect from working people in Casentino. Hard-working, dedicated, and personable. Let’s not forget full of passion. While it was a hard day of work to bring all this stuff into the house, there was always room for fun, admiration and laughs and good times. Our 9m long bench posed a real challenge to the team and equipment, but a different and much bigger truck was brought in to move just one big big beam.

Now there are problems to solve how to get certain machinery for yard work going and keep them going, cutting many of the neglected trees into shape, cutting down some roses, and planting our 1st Fig tree on the property. It is now shaping up to look like a property and a house that is livable. What a good set of issues to resolve. I love it.

Yesterday I managed to finally get the newest member of the team to the house. The 31-year-old Fiat Panda 4x4. Like everything here in Italy, buying it and getting it registered under my name and getting it insured was a little more work-intensive than I expected. But with the right team and dedication, we got that one done as well. 1st car I own in Italy seems to be an Italian Icon.

We managed to get a trip to Florence in, getting Mumu’s suspicion of a skin problem wiped off the table by a Dermatologist and the translating help and recommendation from our hosts. So much love and care are around us. Of course, it works out. How can it not work out? But a trip to the local IKEA made a few more decisions clear and allows us to get the construction started. The contractor/builder has a LATE penalty clause. I insisted on it. He was not worried, neither the Geometra. So far he never had to pay a late penalty, he is not late. I really hope we don’t break his string during the next 3 1/2 months.

We celebrated Mumu's Birthday, which is on the same day as the one of Particia, our host. More great great displays of how to live your life and friendship. SO great to be part of this. I also got introduced to the Casentino MTB crew. There are a lot of bikers out there and the scenery is pretty amazing, the riding is challenging in a technical way as well as just sheer physical ability. ==> It's hard. and I managed to hold on most of the way of the 45km, 1650m climbing route up to Monte Falco and back. Thanks, Silvio, Andrea, and Stefano for riding with me and showing off your trails.

So Mumu and I are back united in California. After a pretty stressful time in Italy to get the next phase of the house purchase accomplished, I slept almost for a day straight afterward, I made my way to California again. December 17th it all started. Hands-on hard work in the Yard to get all the work done that did not happen during the year we tried to rent the house and it was a nightmare, and also nothing got done at all in the yeard. 10 days of hard work for Mumu and me to get only the front and back yard in shape. I totally underestimated the time it would take. We had our favorite painter cover the amazing colors inside with a creamy white. It was hard to see, but it was needed to be able to sell. The inside also needed still a number of changes and we spent maybe a week to get all that done. We moved our matres from the garage into the bedroom and off we went to the Yoga Teacher training we signed up for; 21 days & 8.5 to 10 hours every day talking about Yoga and doing Yoga and teaching Yoga to others. I could not believe it how intense it all was. The group of people there was nothing short of amazing. From all ages and all corners of the world, smart and sensitive people got together to learn about how to teach Yoga to others the best and safest way. It was held in Santa Cruz, but we only got to see a little bit of the sun over lunch and we went back into the studio for some more Yoga talk.

\

Last week we finished all the nitty-gritty in the house to get ready for the stager and photographer. But then it happened, 2 women came to the house and showed interest in the house. Muriel showed them around and they went on their way. In the afternoon the same woman came again, this time with her husband. We walked them through the house and yard again ==> Result was "I want to buy the house". Real Estate agents came into the picture, another visit with the whole family, then an offer was made and we accepted it. We got exactly what we asked for. This all without the house being officially being on the market. Fabulous. -5 days and we have a buyer. -2 days and we have deposit money in the escrow account. WOW. Two more meetings of the buyer's family and agents, still they are very excited to buy. WOW.

\

We now moved out of the house and in with our friends in South San Jose for a week. I finally got a small ride in alone, then today a great hike with my friend Christian in the Milpitas hills. I call it the Qualification Hike. I usually use this one to weed out the slackers when they applied for one of my Trans Sierra speedy hikes. It's pretty long and challenging in terms of climbing. It also was a little "see you later" to the spring green mountains in our area.....

We finally have a kick-off time for our oneyeartrip. So super excited about it all and I can't believe after all the waiting for it, it is now so close.

Mumu will leave for Mexico Dec 25th on a one-way ticket. BIG deal. Mumu quit her job, I have renters for our house, the dog is taken care off for the year, the chickens will have a safe and caring home and bees will have a new playground. We are ready to go!!!

Now the planning part of it all. Which countries at what time, which cities and areas to visit, which trips to do at each location..... Of course, not all will have to be figured out, but some structure will help up along the way.

Mexico will be 1st, the point of this is to calm down and be ready and tuned into what will come next. Some Beach, little activity and lots of quiet. WHERE?

South/Central America will be 1st after Mexico, ==> maybe 2-3 months. It is March by then and we can maybe string one country before we really want to be in Japan for Cherry Blossom and much much more. (Target April 1-15)

I would love to go to Iran, one of the cradles of humanity. I am getting VERY different suggestions on what to do. Travel group, solo, safe - unsafe, .... Some destinations seem to be clear there. Teheran, Isfahan, Yazd, ...

Japan and where to go???

After that, we might want to travel to Europe to check out the areas we might want to settle in. Portugal, Sardinia, Sicily, south of France, Basque area of France near the Pyrenees. Then go to Nuernberg, Germany, maybe some Scandinavian country? Maybe 3 months for that?

Then there is still south east asia to visit and India.

It is not at all defined yet, and as we go further out in time, it is clearly a total unknown.

I am looking forward to the process digging through all this.

We finally have a kick-off time for our oneyeartrip. So super excited about it all and I can’t believe after all the waiting for it, it is now so close.

Mumu will leave for Mexico Dec 25th on a one-way ticket. BIG deal. Mumu quit her job, I have renters for our house, the dog is taken care off for the year, the chickens will have a safe and caring home and bees will have a new playground. We are ready to go!!!

Now the planning part of it all. Which countries at what time, which cities and areas to visit, which trips to do at each location… Of course, not all will have to be figured out, but some structure will help up along the way.

Mexico will be 1st, the point of this is to calm down and be ready and tuned into what will come next. Some Beach, little activity and lots of quiet. WHERE?

I am here, at my sister's place, in her RV since March 15 now. Mumu joined me on March 18th. 6 weeks and counting we are slowly transitioning from way below freezing temperatures here, to now almost Californian standards. For temperatures, that is. We had two short episodes of rain, just a few millimeters of precipitation. It seems to me, Germany is drying out. Blue Sky almost every day. We took our Italian training camp pretty seriously here. Starting from Pizza and Pasta to Aperol Spritz and Campari Orange, Tiramisu, and late-night talks with Family (and no friends). Sewing baking aprons and Corona masks were part of the drill as well. In the times between all this training, I was calling around for establishing Health Insurance (thank you SBK) planing for additional health Coverage (Hanse Merkur and LVM), failing again to transfer money from the USA to the Stadtsparkasse via wire and having to send a paper check here, only to have to wait for 4 (FOUR) weeks for it to hopefully materialize into money in our account here. Then establishing a backup money transfer route with Transferwise and failing because of another US bank restriction. Trying fo the 3rd version of money transfer I am now in possession of a Deutsche Bank account and still hope to get it done with this though the 1st attempt failed again for a missing US connecting bank SWIFT code being needed. The bank official never had to do this before. I will see what Monday will bring on that front. Then some more Italy training, some prosecco and lots of smiles and fun with my sister and husband. Then was a "fee" to pay for our stay. Mow the lawn, carry these pavers from here to there, straighten this driveway, remove the tree, the bush, the roses, ..... So many people tell me they were BORED during the COVID-19 confinement times. No boredom here. I still had to squeeze in my cycling Italy training camp too. I was granted access to my Mom's pretty new 7 speed Bicycle for this task. Not really a speed demon, by any stretch of the imagination. I was able to teach it some new tricks. The bike rack disintegrated in the process but a rubber strap allowed the finish of the ride that day. The fenders started rattling and scratching too loudly to ignore. I could fix it on the fly. After the first few rides feeling really awkward and me being ill-prepared for riding this beast, we are becoming friends now. We make some Mountainbikes roll their eyes when flying down trails way too bumpy for my steel stallion, others huff and puff next to us when we pass them on the way up. Not too many, but it made me happy to create this reaction with the tool available under my butt. Not to forget the Birkenstock as my preferred racing shoes. Always cracks people up. I moved from racing thongs (Flip-Flops) to Birkenstock for temperature reasons.....

\

We are now preparing to enter Italy. Not an easy feat, let me tell you. Mentally as well as organizing it. Our Furniture is already in Poppi. The container arrived and was unloaded ahead of schedule at Decor Tuscany in their warehouse. Now we want to follow to be able to sign the purchase contract on May 19th. Calling around in Germany from one Italian Consulate to the next, I finally spoke to a person. A competent person. There is a real chance we might make it across the border into Italy, but he could not be sure, everything is so dynamic. I will call Thursday next week again, just days before Italy is supposed to slowly open the restrictions a little for business and movement of people. My plan is to rent a car and drive from Nuernberg to Poppi, crossing Austria, and entering Italy. Seems easy during regular times. What will the border patrol people ask us, what documentation will we need to be able to cross these border into Austria and into Italy? Most likely we will be in confinement for 2 weeks after entering Italy and getting to Poppi. We plan to stay on our friends Farm, in our separate house. If we play it right and everything works the way planned, we will be JUST ready to sign the papers for buying the house of our dreams on May 19th. Entry May 4th, 14days confinement ==> May 19th. To be sure we can buy the property, wether we can enter Italy or not, we will establish a Power of Attorney. Francesco would sign for us in this case. All this is only possible because we think we fended off a push from the seller of the house to postpone the sale date of the house. For reasons that can only be labeled unreasonable and maybe even ridiculous, the woman of the sibling selling party wanted to postpone the sale till June 30th or later. Two calls of a lawyer later, we THINK we have her back in line.

Hurdles after hurdles. I am getting a little tired of it now. I just want to move into this place and think about myself, ourselve. Not of Legal, money, Virus, healthcare or any problems. I am DONE with problem-solving for a week or so....Maybe. I hope.

Italy, we are coming, let us in. PLEASE.

We have this tradition to bring good California weather to London, every time we go there. So, what will it be this time?

While Japan was a truly great and fulfilled experience, we were very glad to get to spend some Family time with Cassandre and Gabriele. Doing that under the sun would be so much more fun, so we brought some along. Leaving the futuristic Osaka was not that hard for me.

ASIANA flight was flawless and we arrived tired in their apartment. 5 minutes after great hugs and shower, both Mumu and I went straight to bed. We were SO tired. I got to play with the sourdough starter that Cassandre maintained for a year and kicked off some country loaves. I don't think the 1st one hit the kitchen table for more than one hour till it was gone. I think it must have been really bad bread. I picked up the Brompton from the store and started my mental recovery routine. Riding! Was that a treat to finally ride again and ride a bike that actually fits my body. Mumu and I were able to cook and prepare breakfast for the whole team and spoil the kids a little. How fun is that!? Eating a salad, vegetables and things we can actually pronounce the name of food we eat for a change. Being able to have a conversation with anyone, anywhere. Simple joys of being in England.

 

\

### Rides

I managed to do two rides so far, one to Redwood Park, Heathrow and back along a Canal [LINK1](https://www.strava.com/activities/2388072205https://www.strava.com/activities/2388285283) [LINK2](https://www.strava.com/activities/2388072205), both with the new "relationship saving" Brompton. ;-)

the Second one [LINK](https://www.strava.com/activities/2397151585) was more remote and I needed a train to get to _**Reading**_ and then rode through amazing countryside and incredibly green hills and fields for a few hours. What a mental treat that was.

\

Allison and Nigel invited us to meet in Winchester for a California reunion and tour through the old town, then a small ride with Nigel to an amazing lunch place in the area. What a treat to ride through this area. It felt 100% British riding. I loved to exchange with the two. who moved back to the UK about 2 years ago. Great times.

More cooking for yourself and the "kids" which was a treat as well. I miss it a lot in these times of travel. I managed to do some bread too. So good. But more about that in the next post.  London rocks though, with it's clear opposition to "T".

\

Poppi and more Poppi - Casentino Valley has us back

It's been a long time since my last post. But I made it to Poppi. It is the area we are looking to buy a property.

The temperatures climbing out of the Poo delta, over the Apennines and into the Casentino valley were really warm, but nothing like it was in the plains. I started my ride at 6.00 and it was still ~25C in the area. My navigation APP went CRAZY and guided me north for a while, till I finally pulled the plug and went into manual navigation mode. ==> not all were the best suitable cycling roads and the elevation I rode was more than prescribed. BUT but but. It was beautiful in the area. As soon as I climbed out of the plains, trees started to appear and cars thinned out as I used smaller roads crossing over ridges to get to the roads less traveled. All this search ended up "costing" me 80m extra climbing. These were such beautiful climbs, I would do them again in a heartbeat. The scenery was wide and remote, lots of forests and I was in heaven. To get up Passa Calla was a bit of a workout, but 1/2 liter of wine together with 1.5 liters of water at a little tourist resort gave me the needed patt on the butt to make it up there. A little tipsy but very happy I go to start my descent into the Casentino Valley. 17km of straight and beautiful downhill through the amazing forest, partially part of the National Park of the area. Stia awaited me and with that known territory and streets. After a total of 9 hours, I arrived in Francesco and Lucrezia's place. The timing could not have been better as I arrived just when they started lunch. Heaven was right here. The following morning Francesco got to experience what it looks like when a hungry Stefan eats breakfast. I think I scared him for life. As the dinner the night before was really tiny, I took the liberty to go to town. I think Francesco saw a side of me he has not yet seen. I was the food inhaling monster I tend to be after a hard ride.

Though I wanted to only take 1-2 days rest here and then move on to Apulia, all the way in the south of Italy, I decided it is too hot to move on. I also thought it would be wise to spend some good time in the area we are so much looking forward to buying a house and property. In the mean-time, I helped out Francesco with his BnB and with the party as well as the wedding of Abi and Lorela. A young and well-grounded as well as super lively and diverse couple. He is Brazilian-Japanese and she is Italian-??? living in Sydney and currently in the process of moving back into the Casentino Valley. I helped to serve them, doing this and that, and in the end, we all danced till we could no longer dance. 5am was my final call, but I heard of people going on till 9.30. The following day, all met back up at the pool and tried to get rid of the hang-over. I had so much water, I was fine :-).

After 1 1/2 weeks, I picked up Mumu at Florence airport after getting a rental car. We got our heads together, looked at more property, AGAIN. and discussed and pretended to sleep while thinking all night and more of the same and more..... I think we finally made up our mind to try to spell out an offer for one property. It is the biggest land of all, it is the furthest away from any town and it is the prettiest house we have looked at. Here some pictures of the beauty [LINK](https://photos.app.goo.gl/H1FYybXGJTXmfsJm8).

![Macia-house](/photos/macia-house.png)

Fingers crossed. (Again)

Poppi and more Poppi, rides and a LOT OF RAIN

Google Pictures [LINK](https://photos.app.goo.gl/FLooCuufNzMzcGRb7)

Mumu and I spent some good times in the Casentino Valley, trying to get some rest into our heads as well as doing some early planning for the hopefully soon to be, new house.

I ran into an Australian guy, Dave, at Poggio di Dante and I showed him around some of the roads I know. Only smooth ones of course as he had this exquisite carbon racing machine, skinny tires and understandably not willing to risk a flat. Our 1st stint was a short ride to Talla, ~22km one way and some climbing. I usually take 1hour to get there and another to get back. Well, I seem to have bought the express train option with Dave and we sipped espresso back at his place after 1 1/2 hours only. I showed signs of the effort, Dave was not even phased. Great talks along the way, whenever I was able to spare a breath of two, made it all worth it and really fun. We went on a few more like this and it is truly much better to suffer in company. I only had company when it was not uphill, as dave seems to light a rocket on his side when it is going up. ... You OK is the last thing I hear, and 15 seconds later he is out of sight.

It is clearly turning to be Fall here in the Valley. November is the month of rain here and I think we had more rain in 5 days than we usually have in a whole year in San Jose. There is a reason why Tuscany is so green. Mumu and I were able to squeeze in the one or the other short walk, not hike as we both were downed by some serious COLD bug. I was forced to NAP for 5 days straight, 2 hours each day. We were the coughing and sneezing couple for a while.

We found a rental home for the time we are remodeling the Macia house. A tiny and charming place. The people renting it seem great and very warm. They will not be there most of the time as they live in Florence.

\

Dave and his family were on a similar trip that we. They were out for 6 months as a complete family. House sold, jobs quit and remote schooling for the kids. What an awesome experience for the 4 of them. They seem to really have tuned into each other and set priorities and managed to pull off a trip like that. Amazing to me, and an inspiration for many I hope. The kids will NEVER forget this trip and come out so much bigger and better than how they started the trip.

\

Oh, and Mumu is making good progress on riding the Unicycle. The rain really held up any further progress, but this is moving through the phases fine. We are trying to get some type of rhythm into our day, one item is to try to have a semi-regular Yoga practice per day. The local cats help a lot distracting our minds as well. Mumu found out that cat presence does NOT increase the quietness of mind during Yoga.

![DSC\_0382-S](/photos/dsc_0382-s.jpg)

We have decided to start moving a little as Mumu got "ants in her pants" and could not really stay in the Valley any longer doing almost nothing productive. SO we decided to go to Paris for a week, stay with Vero and Sandrine, then in Manu's place. Thank you for all your hospitality. This is amazing! Take the train to Cassandre and Gabriele for an early Thanksgiving party, then fly to Nuernberg for the opening of the Christmas market and some Marita time for me. Mumu will fly to San Jose one Dec 3rd and trying to get the house ready for sale while I will wait to be able to sign the next phase of the house purchase agreement.

It is pretty amazing to me how much on the edge we too still are. Small things set of one of us easily, I am not quite clear what is going on in my head, but I am not at ease. I think it is the lack of a NEST. It will take about another one year, to get to that nest that we both som much desire.

We moved to Tuscany, Italy in May 2020. It is a move I will find hard to forget. It was a move that we thought about long and hard. It is a move that I am still super excited about and am happy and a little proud we managed to pull of. So so many reasons were and are good, to make a change like this. I am happy we did come here. Here is not only Europe, not only Italy, not only Tuscany. Here is The Casentino Valley. It was also important for us to escape from the USA, from CA, and the Bay Area.
