**Stay at Home**

It is now 4 weeks since I am hunkered down in Nuernberg Germany. Mumu is with me and that is a true blessing. We are still staying with my sister and her husband, in their RV in their yard. We are lucky enough to be within shouting distance of the "Reichswald" and the Northerly direction gives access to the "Fraenkische Schweiz" a Rock climbing paradise and hiking/biking network to dream of. This is now coupled with a very disciplined German society that takes Government imposed restrictions seriously and follows these in most cases. So do we. Only groups that are allowed are with Family members you stay with. You are not allowed to meet ANYONE, not even one outside this circle. Keeping a distance of at least 1.5m, better 2m to anyone at all times is the code of conduct. This is not 100% possible in stores, but most people try hard. The government seems to lead the public exceptionally well. Information is provided with urgency, transparency, and competence. As a result, the people feel being treated as responsible adults and in return respond like responsible adults, MOSTLY. You hear reports about some "Corona parties", and a group that tries to intimidate and distract Police here, but the state does not seem to lose control of the situation. The stores are filled with goods we need to live and live very well. ==> We are not where we want to be, but we feel fortunate to be here and well kept. The case chart shows the result of the measures taken. On top of it all, I was able to get back into the German Health insurance system. It was not easy and took 3 weeks of calls, letters, and emails. But now Mumu and I are again fully Health insured, which seems like one of the main things you want to have today. Transferring the money we need for the house purchase was as painful as it was for the downpayment. I still have to understand what the problem is. But it is on the way to Germany now. Next in line to organize, finalizing the transfer of ownership of the house. With Italy having closed the borders for more than one month, we don't know when or how we can go down to sign for the transfer and move in. We figured out a way to do the signature and payment remotely, if this is necessary, which is a HUGE relief. Come Tuesday, I will try to connect with an Italian Consulate here and see how we can arrange for us to be towards the front of the line as soon as the border opens back up.

![](/photos/corvid-nuernberg-april13-cases.png)

**FUN**

Mumu and I run almost every day a little bit, right here in the area, right from the house. This helps with the thought of being "stuck" and helps with complacency. I discovered I can even have some biking fun with a bike that does not at all fit me and is anything but a performance bike. I am using my Mom's 7-speed city bike and can teach it some new tricks. Biking with Mumu a few times too seems to rub off some two-wheeled excitement ;-). We have also ventured out one day to do a "Via Ferrata" or Klettersteig one day. With one harness for Mumu from the neighbor we ventured out and Mumu was apprehensive before, but now wants to do another one soon. I hope this trend continues. Rock climbing is so much fun and you get to do it at any level and any age. and the risk is virtually zero to get hurt. The area of the "Fraenkische Schweiz" is known for its rock climbing potential and we are just south of it all. Then there is asparagus, another local highlight. It's white asparagus and we happen to be "stuck here" just in the season of it coming out. It is in season only for ~4 weeks and it is truly delicious. My Mom was generous enough to buy enough for all of us, and we had one amazing fulfilling meal. Then we had another asparagus soup the next day and it was an excellent reminder of how good the meal, just 15h before was.

Rock climbing is so much fun and you get to do it at any level and any age. and the risk is virtually zero to get hurt. The area of the “Fraenkische Schweiz” is known for its rock climbing potential and we are just south of it all. Then there is asparagus, another local highlight. It’s white asparagus and we happen to be “stuck here” just in the season of it coming out. It is in season only for ~4 weeks and it is truly delicious. My Mom was generous enough to buy enough for all of us, and we had one amazing fulfilling meal. Then we had another asparagus soup the next day and it was an excellent reminder of how good the meal, just 15h before was.

I am shopping for my Mom, but mostly stay at a distance and out of her house, to keep her as safe as can be. Sometimes a trip to the area for a little hike is needed to keep the ceiling from falling on her head. But she is a smart woman who can take care of herself very well.

Day 46 A great morning in the campground with 8.00 breakfast with pastry and baguette. Then a car ride to the next town, where we managed to geta taxi cab to the next starting point, skipping a while day of the trail that we expect to be especially boring. We climbed a lot, starting only at 12.00 noon, in the heat, but found a lot of shade under truly magnificent trees. They kept changing and still stayed beautiful. We got to Illas with just enough time for a cold shower before dinner was served. Delicious dinner. The town had an unusual and weird touch.

Day 47 After a very weird and witchy might in Illas with dogs barking endlessly and chickens and roosters throughout the whole valley joining in a grand chorus several times throughout the night.... We all were ready to leave this place early. 7.10 departure. The day started already pretty warm but we could test a few times for blackberry break. The scenery is not that great, not bad either though. It took us 4 hours to get down to the valley and freeway Le Perthus. Checking on dinner availability at the next Gite revealed that they are fully booked. This info together with the temperature forecast of 34C tomorrow brought us to a long long group discussion on what to do. Go on our cutting the chords and calling it quit. We decided to move on with caution. Wait till 16.30 - 17.30 today to walk up the 800m to the finish point of the day, then wake up early and stay walking in the dark tomorrow morning to possibly escape the heat or at least be able to manage it. Let's see how all that will play out. Day 48 The final day finally arrived. We got started hiking in the dark at 6.00. A new experience for this trip. It was already warm at this time of the day, and I was a little shocked and fearful of what was to come. Oven, inferno, sauna.... Who knows. The wind was super super strong, that seemed good at the time. It will it be like a hair dryer in our faces inn the afternoon. Who knows how bad the temperature will be. We made good progress and found the one spring that is still active along the way. Impressive bites along the way and another set of views of the so long desired Mediterranean sea. We all were pretty focused on time and temperature do breaks were regular but pretty short. It got really hot and steep towards the end and shaded areas rare. But I'm about 8 hours we managed to complete this monster of a hike and arrive at the Sea, diving in about one minute after arrival. What a treat, what a day, what a journey and experience. We had a nice leftover meal along the beach together then struggled to find a restaurant still servings good at 21.00 and had a night in a hotel, trying to process what just happened

Vino cotto con neve - An Italian experience, truly

![](/photos/img_20260106_161917_997.jpg)

Today it snowed at our house. The first time it snowed here in the last 3 years. So naturally, we went for a walk to town. After not even 15-minute walking, my friend Natale called, and I went to see him at his mom's house for some coffee. Well, that was an Italian inviting around lunch time, for a coffee…. You know what that means. More. I get there, get to eat a full lunch, cooked by Paola, his mom, and it was Italian, great and amazing. Then I hoped for my promised coffee, but I was wrong again. Up comes her neighbour with a small bottle in her hand. Brown thick liquid inside. My friend Natale disappeared for a few minutes and came back with a pot of fresh snow, right from outside. What's going on? And while they all talk Italian really really fast, and I don't understand much, I keep hearing "Vino Cotto". I translated this to mulled wine or Glühwein. But I was so wrong. Then the snow was put into glasses, and the brown liquid poured on top. The brown liquid is cooked down from grape juice. Then you stir the mix, and like magic, it all transforms into a sorbet-like consistency. Then you spoon it up, and you get to ingest one of maybe the earliest sorbets of this world. The real earliest of this dessert seems to come from China and Persia.

Not only was this a very unique and a first time for me, but between Natale, an art historian and a sommelier for wine, and his mom, who has been living since 85+ years, an d both have never eaten this.

Walking alone as a woman - what I see and how I feel about it

Yesterday I went on one of my Unicycle rides, alone, this time in the Oakland hills in the Chabot Park area. Clearly, I am a man, I am tall and I probably come across as confident. I don't think I come across as dominant or threatening or as a womanizer. I am sitting on a UNIcycle that I would expect to put me a little out of the norm of the general threatening male parties, in the eyes of a woman; I think, I hope that is true. So I am on my way for the short ride I have in mind and I happen to meet two different women along the trail, both walking their dogs. The fact that really shocked me was the impression I got from both of them as I come closer. I clearly sensed "I am scared of you" what will you do in the next 10seconds, do I need to defend myself? and more and more. I ended up quickly asking one of the two women for the way, trying my best not to look at her too long, stating I am almost on my way back and looking away as much as I found reasonable. And the impression did not change much at all, I don't think I made the feeling any better, I am very sorry. [![](/photos/image1.png)](/photos/image1.png)

One my way back up the hill, I had enough time to think about what just happened, what situation I was in, what impressions I might have caused. It really made me feel very sad and it brought home to me one more time how women have to look at their direct environment, at people and the street ahead of them, at people they might encounter or cross paths with in the next few minutes. I pretty much never have to do this and used to take this for granted and in the last few years more and more had to realize how different my view of the world is, and how lucky I am to be born as a buy a man and also white. ## TransAlp

So I did this thing called TransAlp in August. A big word for some, meaning nothing to most. For me I saw it as a vehicle to get something done in my head. After 2 years of remodeling and reconstruction projects of our new home in Tuscany my brain was tired. Really tired and it showed effects on how I react to situations and interact with others. I decided in the spring,

_Stefan needs a reset, re-callibration, mental grounding,.... I needed some real time off_.

I wanted to be in nature, still with people. I wanted to shut up for a while, while still being around people. I wanted to be alone, but not all alone. I wanted to do something, without having to plan a whole lot, without having to organize stuff. I wanted a simple time. Simple for me, predictable to a certain degree, enough chances for stuff to go wrong a little bit, so I can get myself back out of it. --> So I decided to put one foot in front of the other and do that for a while, do that for a long while. As I have done plenty of Trans Sierra trips in California, a TransAlp seemed appropriate. For the not so athletically inspired, a TransAlp is a crossing of the Alps by the strength of your own body. You can do it any way you want, by foot, by bike, on skies, paragliding, hang-gliding, .... or any other sport, or mix between them. I had the idea of doing this crossing the Alps as well as attaching a short 6 day hike from Bologna back home to it, for good measure.

## **Planning**

Where do I cross, which path do I take, which huts do I go to, how high do I want to be, how difficult do I want this thing to be, and much could be decided ahead of time, the route nailed down, saved on my phone and I would have a pretty simple life for a while. Well, I actually could attach a segment in the Apennine mountain range tot he end of this TransAlp and walk right back home. Done deal. I have a rough plan. Who is coming? Well, who wants to do such a thing AND can take off more than one month for this AND can handle me for all this time and not smack me in the face every day for being so stupid to go on a hike like this? WHO? Well I was lucky and found two fabulous people, Ralf and Manuela. Both with the right attitude to such an endeavor and the body to do it. The logistics were figured out pretty quickly and the trip was ready to start. Right after Cassandre's and Gabri's wedding in London we took off. July 28, Thursday, 7.20 the train left Nuernberg with Ralf and me. We picked up Manuela in Allersberg and were in Munich only 1 1/2 hours later. A short S-Bahn ride later we were at our starting point just north of Lenggries, about 60km south of Munich. A brief lunch at the "Brezelstuben" and we were off on our trip. The destination for the 1st part of this trip was Lago di Garda in Italy, not knowing what would happen along the way and how things would change. I read from other people and other adventures; plan your trip, read about it, give yourself options along the way, know your route, ..... Then, once it starts, be ready to change it all the 1st day.

![](/photos/my-pack-s.jpg)

![](/photos/we-start-s.jpg)

## No, Yes, Maybe, Why

I don't want to write a whole recap of the trip here. Maybe I do that later. I want to write about what happened during the trip. I have never done a trip doing biking, riding or otherwise for such a long time. I was pretty certain my legs and rest of the body would be up for this. I was not so certain how it would work with my head. I wanted to calm this thing down, I wanted to come out the other side of this trip better than I went in. People told me all kinds of things.

- After one week your body is used to it and all will be fine.

- Are you crazy, why would you do that to yourself.

- I would get bored after 2-3 days.

- You will be so relaxed after this, I want to go too.

- What if X,Y,Z happens....

And of course, it all came totally different. I had a terrible 1st night. My belly rebelled, I could not sleep, I had a screaming headache ( I never have headaches). As a result I felt terrible the 1st day and had to nurse myself through the day. I was able to hike the 2nd day. I was weak, needed to cough, could not eat, barely drank anything. Next night was good, but the following day barely better. ==> Doubts came up in my mind. Are you really up for this? Why are you doing this? Day 3 was much better but I was still far from being myself. In the meantime, it rained every day, from "not much" up to "2-3 hours and really hard". That did not help me, but I muddled through and on day 5 or so, I was able to walk at a speed uphill again that I knew I could and I wanted to. I was still not at 100% but the body felt good enough to proceed. This "unproductive cough" stuck with me till the very end of this adventure.

One short statistic. We hiked ~420km and climbed ~20.000m in the process. It took us 29 days to do that.

## What happened in that head?

But something happened during this time. I could see a certain rhythm in our days and it was comforting. We get up at 6.30, start hiking at 7.30 or 8.00 latest. Then we hike till about 14.00 to 17.00 at the longest and where done. Some days it would be a little tricky to find the route, some days we had more technical terrain, some others we would have to climb up steep hills just to go back down the other side, some days it would rain a little more, some others it would be warm. At the end of the day, we would arrive in one piece, in a good mood and nicely tiered, between 14.00 and 17.00 in the afternoon, would eat some cake and have a beer at the hut, eat dinner, chat with fellow hikers or not and go to bed. The next morning all this would repeat. We all stopped worrying about the details of the route of the day, will it be too hard for us, will we make it over this pass, or that decent. It wold all work out till the afternoon and it would be good. This was a pretty neat rhythm. What of this could or would I want to transfer to my regular life? How can I enter every day now, as i am back home and be able to be as happy and content with every evening, going to bed nicely tired, not worrying about much. Then I only worried about if my bed neighbor will be snoring that night (earplugs or not).

## Take something home, Stefan

I want to take some part "home" from this. What can I learn from this?

At least in concept, I want to be able to take this contentness and easy going mind set with me. I think it could help me be happier, lead a little lighter life.

* * *

I tend to think and optimize things a lot, try to predict what all could come from doing it this way vs. that way. I am not a worrier, but I think about the impact my actions have on others, how others actions might impact me a lot. Maybe some of this can be reduced. Maybe, just maybe.

**Others**: I try to influence people I care about. I try to take an interest in the direction they seem to take, ..... All this, while it is well meant, and it got me to the state in my life is taking a toll on me. All this takes a lot of effort on my side and I have to say, only very few things I stated to others actually resulted in a directional change from them. It was just that I cared so much about them. Why would I not say something, at the right time, the right way...... I did not do that during the 4 weeks and life went on.  
I only speak this out because I care, it only gets ignored because others don't usually want to hear it, don't want to talk about it or what ever other reason.

**Me**: I can't say that I care a huge amount what others think of me. I do, but I don't really. I think I want to take this attitude of easy going, accepting what comes, seeing a top level rhythm in my days weeks and months. That does not seem that easy to me. Not easy to get to easy.

1st step: No-one shall get my well meant advice, and probably, no-one will notice.

2nd step: I have to think about that one, but I will start with a nightly listing of all the good/bad things that happened to me that day, how it is similar to the day before, and not think what I might do tomorrow. Maybe I can find this pattern in my days, maybe I can trust in the flow there is and just go with it. Go with the flow and see where it is taking me. There is so so so much talk about that going around.

- let the force be with you

- follow the flow

- see where life carries you

- when you'r falling - dive

Many concepts that seem quiet similar.

I am happy I did this, I think it worked out for me, I can only highly recommend it to anyone that needs to clear the head. Choose what seems right for you, don't copy what I or someone else did.

We are starting ---a long process -- Porchiano might get 2 new weird ones

Google Pictures [LINK](https://photos.app.goo.gl/VkaUGMdBxkj8evcd9)

We have submitted an offer and it was accepted with some conditions and tweaks. It is a long process with many possibilities of falling through, but it is another step in the right direction. In the direction of us 2 settling in the Casentino Valley. I will NOT praise the night before the FAT lady sings. But I will say we both are very happy about where we are. Let the project begin.

In the meantime, Mumu is here with me and the French Family arrived here too for a week of vacation before we go and check out Sicily for 3 weeks.

Last week I prepared for a group ride up Pratomagno, one of the highest mountains h=in the area. Mumu wanted to ride up and our hosts, Lucrezia and Francesco joined in as well. I rode up the day before to check out the best roads and see how far the "E-Bike" crew will make it in this area. It was smart to do that as some roads were pretty rough on the gravel side and the route had way more intensity that I think would have been appreciated by the team. 1st lap done on this climb, Thursday, all 4 of us went out on Friday with 3 E-Bikes and my "S" drive (Stefan drive). I was LAST on the climbing for a change this time. We took our time with several stops to look at houses and to have a little snack along the way in Quora. Lucrezia managed to run out of E-Bike battery 1km before the summit. The price you pay for passing us all in Turbo mode every time. Mumu and I managed to get to the Cross of Pratomagno, then back down the same way we came. It is an impressive view from up there, we were chased back down by the looming clouds and thunder around us. The best thing was that Mumu really enjoyed the ride, and it might be a great way to do these things together.

And what a great day to send together with our hosts since more than 5 weeks this year.

**Yesterday Dec 13th** we finally signed the most committing document of this transaction. Preliminary sales agreement. Stepping away from this would be very very expensive for both parties, and by the look of all involved, no one will. The days and hours leading up to it were eventful and hectic, even more than I expected. Doing to the bank for money matters two times, finding possibly illegal fence lines on the property (which ended up being fine and good for us), incorrect basic math by the real estate girl and lack of some prior payment records filled my days and hours before Friday 15.30 with more than I bargained for. Then 4 hours at the Notaio with two witnesses, and interpreter for me (she was fine and things worked out, but she was anything but qualified for this job), listening one of the two sellers (a lawyer herself) arguing with the Notario about one or the other wording with true Italian passion, then me listening to the Notario reading it Lloyd 32 pages of contact detail, making corrections as we went and argued. DONE I thought. But no, the next hour was filled with editing the just finished document and reprinting it, then, without any more reading we "blindly" trusted the edits and signed. What a wild ride. I am sure it will all work out, but the process employed is not at all waterproof. The next milestone is deed transfer and therefore full ownership. May 19, 2020. I discovered 20-30 Walnut trees and 5 Hazelnut trees and more land that we will own. I am not kidding, this land is huge. Walking from one edge to the other is more than 500m. May the force be with us...

Google [Pictures](https://photos.app.goo.gl/WUZkv77i997Hnekj8) **ENGLISH** SHORT POST!! Here in Southern Patagonia, I have to say that weather does really really matter. On so many days you could say, "If you don't like the weather, wait a minute" and some others the rain clouds just stay with you, for the day. And we managed to experience one of these rain days while NOT on a trip but in El Calafate. Les vélos de ville BA ne sont pas les meilleurs, mais les meilleurs que je puisse avoir à temps. Il faisait 30 ° C et plat, mais 6 km sur une selle de cruizer n’était pas un pur plaisir.

Notre dernier jour ici, nous avons passé en Uruguay - Colonia del Sacramento. À seulement une heure de bateau, nous avons passé une journée dans cette petite ville au rythme lent, plongeant dans les eaux douces du fleuve Uruguay. C’est assez touristique et lent. Y aller une fois était sympa. Je ne pense pas que je dois y retourner. MAIS, j’avais mon premier compagnon là-bas. Une boisson intéressante à coup sûr. J’aime que cela semble vraiment être une chose régionale à faire et à boire. Tout le monde semble l’apporter n’importe où. Voyons si je tombe dans le goût de celui-ci.

Demain, nous ferons notre dernier saut vers le sud. Ce sera le sud ainsi que loin des villes pendant un moment. Tout au sud. Je pense que ce sera un choc pour tous nos systèmes. Nous allons laisser tomber beaucoup de température. 1C pour chaque 100 km qui est. Nous partons d’ici à une température de 32 ° C et nous y arriverons sous des averses de neige ….. 2 à 5 ° C. Allons-y. Ushuaia.

What to do when a car and driver threatens you on the road

I had a pretty traumatic experience yesterday and I am still in the process of digesting it. I am writing this, in part to work through it. I am still nervous, a little scared and not sure what to do next to try and avoid situations like this. Here it goes.

I am riding my bike to Yoga on Monday, June 18th. This SUV passes me and another cyclist pretty close on Julian Street, at the underpass of Caltrain. This is always an area that I am trying to avoid as it leaves no escape for cyclists when cars and drivers don't leave enough room to the side. Both of us (cyclists) seem pretty annoyed by this event and have a brief visual contact. We keep riding to the next intersection (Alameda) and see the same SUV there as well. I pull onto the SUVs driver side and knock on his window to get the drivers attention, as he is seemingly trying to avoid looking at me. I tell him that his recent passing of me was really close and not safe, through the closed driver side window. I get a middle finger pointed in my direction as a response. The fellow cyclist says something as well in my direction, but I don't recall what. The light turns green and the SUV takes off making a left turn. I stay behind him, as not to get caught in anything. The SUV now dulls really fast to the right side of the road as to block my passing on his right side. I am pulling out my cellphone and take a picture of his license plate, then proceed to pass his SUV slowly on the left side as he has to wait at the red light. Profanities are being sent my way by the driver. At this point, the lights turn green and I am opting to proceed on the sidewalk as not to get into physical danger by the erratic driving style. More profanities coming my way, not better or worse ones, just repeats of the same. But the driver is now asking me to stop so we can have a fight. I decline and state I have never fought anyone in my life, he will not be the 1st. More threatening statements are coming my way; "I have a full tank of gas, I will follow you to your home, I will watch out for you every day from now on along this route and this time, I will hunt you down, you better watch out from now on ...... My riding has to be careful as not to be in the front of him or giving him any chance to pinch off my ride between road and curb as I am weaving from the left side of the road's sidewalk to the right side's sidewalk. My goal now is to get to a more public place, get inside a building with more people and hopefully discourage him from following me any further. After a few left-right turns I finally arrive at the entry of Nu-Life Yoga, I enter and that was the last I see of him.........

## **so far.**

White supremacy, and why I truly think and know it is .....

I hear about [David Duke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Duke), a man who almost made it into the US senate, \[**CORRECTION**: was Governor of Luisiana\] made it into the house of Representatives in Luisiana and who made it his trademark to “**_look after the white_** _**race**_” and protect the world from inferior mindsets, preventing the mingling and mixing of humans of different origins and races.

I thought about this a lot and why I am so fundamentally opposed to it.

What makes me think this purist approach is so bad. Purist meaning, one group, sticking to itself, doing it's own thing can be better than groups mixing among each other. Who am I to judge someone's opinion and conviction without stomping on others' rights and beliefs? White supremacy is clearly proposing that the "white race" is better than the "black race". So I 1st thought I need to prove to myself that this is not true, find studies that show this fact. Well, I think it would still be a very weak argument in my view. It would still be a true argument, don't get me wrong. But I think it just compares one set of studies to another set of studies. ==> This will not get my point across big enough. I think the whole theory that ONE RACE will be better than a MIXED RACE is flawed. I am of course opposed to the fundamental idea that there is such a thing as supremacy of any race or any group of people.

I think I can prove that the mixing of all people is so much better than “sticking to our own kind”?

I want to go one level up. I want to step back and see which teams or groups in my professional life were successful and which ones were not. I am trying to augment the mix of the people of a team with respect to the quality of result they produce. Let’s make this simple by proposing a project.

**PROJECT**: We want to have a plan for the design and implementation of a pedestrian bridge over a busy street in the middle of a city.

Which team comes up with the best solution?

- Is a team with only structural engineers coming up with the best possible solution for this project?
    
- Is it a team with only structural engineers together with some leading experts in this area that have built these bridges over the last 30 years already?
    
- Is it a team with structural engineers together with members from the community, a kindergarten teacher, a few teenagers, members of the elderly community, a baker, a long-distance runner, an astronaut, a person in a wheelchair, a nanny and a member of the last bridge design that was a complete failure.
    

One would think that the team of expert engineers will come up with the best solutions. They know their subject matter, the group is small and agile and will come up with the solution fast, efficient and will get it right. They will be sure that their solution is the best and come out with confidence and come out with a great plan for that pedestrian bridge.

One would also initially think that the idea of bringing people into the team that have failed in previous projects would be a really stupid idea. After all, they messed up the last design, why would I give them a chance to mess up another one again. That is stupidity, no?

What good can a group of complete novices in this field of bridge design do to this team? This is overhead and will only bring this project to a grinding halt, slow it down unnecessarily. This is crazy talk to set up a team like this. We are designing a bridge, this is not a coffee and cake party.

Mixed gender team [LINK](https://www.trainingjournal.com/articles/opinion/why-mixed-gender-management-teams-perform-better)

Diverse team setup [LINK](https://bmchealthservres.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s12913-018-3812-4) [LINK](https://thenextweb.com/entrepreneur/2019/04/10/why-diverse-teams-make-better-business-decisions/)

To me as well as it is shown in these studies, it is a proven fact that the setup of the team is critically important to the ultimate success of the project. Also the mix of knowledge and experience, the wide variety of points of view makes the team stronger and better. The simplistic view of experts produce the best solutions is flawed. Why would I even want a _**pure**_ race, a _**pure**_ country, a _**pure**_ city. Why **pure** when you can have a mix?

In truth the purist and elitist approach is only about elevating yourself. It's about fulfilling one's need of power over others.

I have heard, thought and talked a lot about what goes on throughout the US, Europe as well as the world with the spread of the isolationist view of life. In politics, business and more. Isolating and elevating yourself from others seems to go on for more and more people in the last years.

It not only will lead us into some simplistic bubble, but also down a cliff of violence and even more wars and injustice. How do we change that.... I have no idea. I found it important to me to think about it and come to a thought through conclusion.

THINK and you can discuss. FOLLOW and you will only talk.

Google Photos [LINK](https://photos.app.goo.gl/As4GxY4BhSgsBLsA7) **ENGLISH** I was (almost) speechless when I saw the lake districts views just north of San Carlos De Bariloche. It is towards the northern - western end of Patagonia and the landscape changed pretty dramatically from the more gently rising glacier created hills and valleys further south, the Steppe and the dessert style vegetation. **_Lake Nahuel Huapi_** is long and deep and wide, it is not round like Lake Tahoe, but it has about the same surface area and is almost as deep. But to the coastline is about 5X the length. The colors of it are amazing and you can easily find your private spot to enjoy. Even in one of the BUSY Beach areas, there are barely 20-30 people around. And both Mumu and I were impressed by the views and had to take a dip and another one. The water is maybe a little colder than Tahoe, but maybe not. There are almost no boats on this lake, it is so quiet, even on the beach, you can hear one of the few boats come across from many kilometers away. Impressed, at pease, pleased and happy would start the list of words to describe how I felt. Then there is one more lake and one more lake and one more.... 12 lakes strung up along a street and it was an awesome day to see them all. Well done, well done. - ![](/photos/dsc04031-s.jpg) - ![](/photos/dsc04034-s.jpg) - ![](/photos/dsc04039-s.jpg) Some streets are only Gravel, most are sealed and well done. DRIVERS, well, they are a little short fused I have to say. Not like Italian or Paris drivers! But not laid back in any way. So, we went to Colonia Suiza, expecting... well a Swiss enclave in Patagonia, Argentina. Not so fast, buddy. Don't waste your time and stay on the main road. A pitty-full show of very few somewhat Swiss items in a very dusty and tourist atmosphere. Pfuiii. Then the highlight, a visit to the Cervecería Patagonia [LINK](https://goo.gl/maps/w56hsBgxbH12). While it is a pretty corporate run place with clearly some real money being invested here, it is an amazing spot to serve good beer and food. The views are simply 10.5 out of 10. Hands down, no arguing. They served a "Patagonia 24.7" beer there that was good and the name tickled my interest. Reason for the name is that it was 1st created and brewed at this brewery that is located on kilometer 24.7 of the Circuito Chico. On the circuit, if you only stay in your car, it is not that thrilling. By getting your ass out and hike at a few spots, only 1-2km each, you get to see some pretty great views of this lake area. Or better, rent a bike and ride it, then hike it. - - I am carrying around this lingering cold since a few days now, try to shake it. But it does not really flare up to become a real cold, neither does it go out of my way. Maybe a little hike will get it out of my system. I wanted to do a real killer, barn burner hike, but with that cold, I will not risk it. I would have LOVED that one. I am pretty sure. ~34km and about 1500-2000m climbing, great scenery, Refugios along the way, some class 4 routes ... I will miss out! [LINK](https://www.wikiloc.com/hiking-trails/travesia-villa-catedral-refugio-frey-refugio-san-martin-jakob-tambo-de-baez-22873254) But I will get to hike the shorter version [LINK](https://www.gaiagps.com/datasummary/track/15d04149-5d00-4c6b-968b-0ab87ba05b79/) with my MUMU. Oh, and we have a few Lombard Streets here. Not as long as the one in SF, but some are STEEP. Bariloche has a Swiss influence in its buildings. More importantly, they seem to have adopted the love of chocolate from the Swiss here. [LINK](https://www.authenticfoodquest.com/bariloche-argentina-little-switzerland-and-chocolate/) Rapanui is a known destination but I felt more like in a Starbucks than in a Great Chocolate place. We will try Torres next. **GERMAN** Ich war (fast) sprachlos, als ich die Aussicht auf den See nördlich von San Carlos De Bariloche sah. Es liegt am nordwestlichen Ende von Patagonien und die Landschaft hat sich dramatisch verändert, und zwar durch die sanfter ansteigenden Gletscherhügel und Täler weiter südlich, die Steppe und die Vegetation im Dessertstil. Der Nahuel-Huapi-See ist lang und tief und breit, er ist nicht rund wie Lake Tahoe, aber er hat ungefähr die gleiche Oberfläche und ist fast so tief. Aber an der Küste ist etwa 5X die Länge. Die Farben sind erstaunlich und Sie können ganz einfach Ihren privaten Platz zum Genießen finden. Selbst in einem der belebten Strandbereiche gibt es kaum 20 bis 30 Personen. Und sowohl Mumu als auch ich waren beeindruckt von den Aussichten und mussten ein paar Mal eintauchen. Das Wasser ist vielleicht etwas kälter als Tahoe, aber vielleicht nicht. Es gibt fast keine Boote an diesem See, es ist so ruhig, selbst am Strand kann man hören, dass eines der wenigen Boote aus vielen Kilometern Entfernung kommt. Beeindruckt, froh und zufrieden, würde die Liste der Wörter beginnen, um zu beschreiben, wie ich mich fühlte. Dann gibt es noch einen See und noch einen See und noch einen…. 12 Seen reichten an einer Straße entlang und es war ein großartiger Tag, sie alle zu sehen. Gut gemacht, gut gemacht. Einige Straßen sind nur Kies, die meisten sind versiegelt und gut gemacht. DRIVER, na ja, sie sind ein bisschen kurz, ich muss sagen. Nicht wie italienische oder Pariser Fahrer! Aber nicht in irgendeiner Weise zurückgelegt. Also gingen wir nach Colonia Suiza und erwarteten eine Schweizer Enklave in Patagonien, Argentinien. Nicht so schnell, Kumpel. Verschwenden Sie keine Zeit und bleiben Sie auf der Hauptstraße. Eine pikante Show mit sehr wenigen etwas Schweizer Artikeln in einer sehr staubigen und touristischen Atmosphäre. Pfuiii. Dann das Highlight, ein Besuch im Cervecería Patagonia LINK. Es ist zwar ein hübscher Firmenlaufplatz, in den eindeutig echtes Geld investiert wird, aber es ist ein toller Ort, um gutes Bier und gutes Essen zu servieren. Die Ansichten sind einfach 10,5 von 10 Punkten. Zweifellos, ohne zu streiten. Dort wurde ein „Patagonia 24.7“ -Bier serviert, das gut war und der Name weckte mein Interesse. Grund für den Namen ist, dass er in dieser Brauerei, die sich auf Kilometer 24,7 des Circuito Chico befindet, als erstes geschaffen und gebraut wurde. Wenn Sie auf der Rennstrecke nur in Ihrem Auto bleiben, ist das nicht so aufregend. Wenn Sie Ihren Hintern rausholen und an einigen Stellen (jeweils nur 1-2 km) wandern, sehen Sie einige schöne Ausblicke auf das Seengebiet. Oder besser, leihen Sie sich ein Fahrrad und fahren Sie es dann wandern. Steigen Sie aus dem Auto und wandern Sie ein wenig Holen Sie sich ein Bier, genießen Sie die herrliche Aussicht Ich trage diese anhaltende Erkaeltung seit ein paar Tagen, versuche sie zu schütteln. Aber es flammt nicht wirklich auf, um eine echte Erkältung zu werden, und geht mir auch nicht aus dem Weg. Vielleicht bringt es eine kleine Wanderung aus meinem System. Ich wollte einen echten Killer machen, eine Scheunenbrennerwanderung, aber bei dieser Erkältung werde ich es nicht riskieren. Ich hätte das geliebt. Ich bin ziemlich sicher. ~ 34km und ca. 1500-2000m Klettern, tolle Landschaft, Refugios entlang der Strecke, einige Routen der Klasse 4 … Ich werde es verpassen! LINK Ich werde jedoch mit meinem MUMU die kürzere Version von LINK wandern. Oh, und wir haben hier ein paar Lombardstraßen. Nicht so lange wie die in SF, aber einige sind STEEP. Lombard Street in Bariloche Bariloche hat einen Schweizer Einfluss in seinen Gebäuden. Noch wichtiger ist, dass sie die Liebe zur Schokolade von den Schweizern übernommen haben. LINK Rapanui ist ein bekanntes Ziel, aber ich fühlte mich eher wie in einem Starbucks als in einem großen Schokoladenort. Wir werden Torres als nächstes versuchen. **FRENCH** J'étais (presque) bouche bée quand j'ai vu la vue sur les districts lacustres juste au nord de San Carlos De Bariloche. C’est vers l’extrémité nord-ouest de la Patagonie et le paysage a changé de façon spectaculaire en raison des collines et des vallées plus glaciales qui se dressent plus au sud, de la steppe et de la végétation des desserts. Le lac Nahuel Huapi est long, profond et large, il n’est pas rond comme le lac Tahoe, mais il a à peu près la même superficie et est presque aussi profond. Mais à la côte est environ 5X la longueur. Ses couleurs sont incroyables et vous pouvez facilement trouver votre espace privé. Même dans l'une des zones de plage occupée, il y a à peine 20-30 personnes autour. Et Mumu et moi avons été impressionnés par la vue et avons dû prendre un bain et un autre. L'eau est peut-être un peu plus froide que Tahoe, mais peut-être pas. Il n'y a presque pas de bateaux sur ce lac, il est si calme, même sur la plage, vous pouvez entendre l'un des rares bateaux arriver à plusieurs kilomètres de distance. Impressionné, heureux, heureux et heureux de commencer la liste de mots décrivant ce que je ressentais. I was (almost) speechless when I saw the lake districts views just north of San Carlos De Bariloche. It is towards the northern - western end of Patagonia and the landscape changed pretty dramatically from the more gently rising glacier created hills and valleys further south, the Steppe and the dessert style vegetation.

Lake Nahuel Huapi is long and deep and wide, it is not round like Lake Tahoe, but it has about the same surface area and is almost as deep. But to the coastline is about 5X the length. The colors of it are amazing and you can easily find your private spot to enjoy. Even in one of the BUSY Beach areas, there are barely 20-30 people around. And both Mumu and I were impressed by the views and had to take a dip and another one. The water is maybe a little colder than Tahoe, but maybe not. There are almost no boats on this lake, it is so quiet, even on the beach, you can hear one of the few boats come across from many kilometers away. Impressed, at pease, pleased and happy would start the list of words to describe how I felt.

Then there is one more lake and one more lake and one more… 12 lakes strung up along a street and it was an awesome day to see them all. Well done, well done.

Some streets are only Gravel, most are sealed and well done. DRIVERS, well, they are a little short fused I have to say. Not like Italian or Paris drivers! But not laid back in any way.

So, we went to Colonia Suiza, expecting… well a Swiss enclave in Patagonia, Argentina. Not so fast, buddy. Don’t waste your time and stay on the main road. A pitty-full show of very few somewhat Swiss items in a very dusty and tourist atmosphere. Pfuiii.

Then the highlight, a visit to the Cervecería Patagonia LINK. While it is a pretty corporate run place with clearly some real money being invested here, it is an amazing spot to serve good beer and food. The views are simply 10.5 out of 10. Hands down, no arguing. They served a “Patagonia 24.7” beer there that was good and the name tickled my interest. Reason for the name is that it was 1st created and brewed at this brewery that is located on kilometer 24.7 of the Circuito Chico. On the circuit, if you only stay in your car, it is not that thrilling. By getting your ass out and hike at a few spots, only 1-2km each, you get to see some pretty great views of this lake area. Or better, rent a bike and ride it, then hike it.

I am carrying around this lingering cold since a few days now, try to shake it. But it does not really flare up to become a real cold, neither does it go out of my way. Maybe a little hike will get it out of my system. I wanted to do a real killer, barn burner hike, but with that cold, I will not risk it. I would have LOVED that one. I am pretty sure. ~34km and about 1500-2000m climbing, great scenery, Refugios along the way, some class 4 routes … I will miss out! LINK But I will get to hike the shorter version LINK with my MUMU.

Oh, and we have a few Lombard Streets here. Not as long as the one in SF, but some are STEEP.

Bariloche has a Swiss influence in its buildings. More importantly, they seem to have adopted the love of chocolate from the Swiss here. LINK Rapanui is a known destination but I felt more like in a Starbucks than in a Great Chocolate place. We will try Torres next.

Die Küche ist so gut angelegt und fertig, Jeff, der Besitzer, bringt mich in echte Schwierigkeiten, da ich bereits weiß, dass ich sowas bauen muss … irgendwann bald. Mumu wird dafür sorgen.

Yelapa scheint eine recht kleine und eng zusammengewachsene Gemeinschaft zu sein. Die Menschen, die dort leben, schienen aufrichtig und freundlich zu sein, sie brauchen sich überhaupt keine Sorgen um irgendeinen Zeitplan zu machen. Wir haben hier echte Charaktere getroffen.

**English**

We stayed in Bariloche for a week. It was high season for the area. We want to rent a car. You guessed it, no more cars from international as well as local rental shops. Then our BnB host jumps in and plays her connections. **Voila,** we have a car for 3 days. It allowed us to do the two trips to the Lakes region as I described before. Really beautiful. Then the Circuito Chico and the amazing Patagonia Brewery setup. Then I got really sick with a cold and felt terrible, weak and all that jazz. Mumu and I managed to get our butts out any way to go on the trail I wanted to do. Refugio Del Frey. I managed to do about 1/2 the distance and we had to turn back, Mumu was ready to do much more. The wind hauled at lake level. The park seemed like well-taken care off and offered really great views of the lakes and area. We went back to the Studio and I had a nap instead..... What a loss that was not to hike it all the way as I planned.

We really enjoyed being able to cook for ourself and eat what we felt we needed, not what someone put on the menu. Stability, it's needed in our life and I keep realizing how much of it I do need as well. Regular morning process to go to the great Derilante Coffee house and enjoy their brew was a true treat. We needed to plan our next steps in Chile and start Bolivia ideas, then we needed to have a 1st timing for EU and what will happen and roughly when. This 1-year travel is more involved than I initially thought. Lot's to plan and organize, even if you don't want to plan it ALL out.

The last day in Bariloche was spent with a truly touristy trip up Cerro Otto with a Gondola. YES, I rode the Gondola up AND down. It was mentally very hard for me. All these things to do out there and hike and I can barely get one foot in front of the other. We were surprised to learn where the **REAL** original of DAVID statue is really sown. On top of Cerro Otto. No really ;-)

The trip up north to Mendoza, the dessert and Malbec region was next.

It will be our LAST day in Argentina. We are in a little suburb town called Chacras. It is just south of Mendoza and not a place I would normally visit, but it was good as a one-day stopover on our way to Chile.

I used a few tools for weather and finding our way.

- Clima.com **APP** is detailed and seemed more reliable to me than Wunderground.
- windguru.com **website** was by far the best prediction on what will happen the next few days. The interface is something to get used to. It's a lot of data to digest.
- Maps.me **APP** is a well designed off-line map APP that saves you data, or enables you to find your destination without internet coverage. The only negative thing about this is that the map is missing a bunch of places that interested us.

**German**

Wir waren für eine Woche in Bariloche. Es war Hochsaison für die Gegend. Wir möchten ein Auto mieten. Sie haben es erraten, keine Autos mehr von internationalen und lokalen Mietgeschäften. Dann springt unser BnB-Host ein und spielt ihre Verbindungen. Voila, wir haben ein Auto für 3 Tage. Es erlaubte uns, die beiden Reisen in die Seenregion zu unternehmen, wie ich sie zuvor beschrieben habe. Richtig schön. Dann der Circuito Chico und die erstaunliche Patagonia Brewery-Einrichtung. Dann wurde ich wirklich krank und fühlte mich schrecklich, schwach und all den Jazz. Mumu und ich schafften es, unseren Hintern jeden möglichen Weg zu beschreiten, den ich wollte. Refugio Del Frey. Ich habe ungefähr die Hälfte der Distanz geschafft und wir mussten umkehren, Mumu war bereit, noch viel mehr zu tun. Der Wind zog auf Seehöhe. Der Park schien gut aufgehoben zu sein und bot wirklich großartige Ausblicke auf die Seen und die Umgebung. Wir gingen zurück ins Studio und stattdessen machte ich ein Nickerchen … Was für ein Verlust war es nicht, es so zu machen, wie ich es geplant hatte.

Wir haben es wirklich genossen, für uns selbst kochen zu können und zu essen, was wir für nötig gehalten haben, nicht das, was jemand auf die Speisekarte gesetzt hat. Stabilität, das ist in unserem Leben notwendig, und ich weiß immer wieder, wie viel davon auch ich brauche. Der morgendliche Prozess, zum großartigen Derilante-Kaffeehaus zu gehen und das Gebräu zu genießen, war ein wahrer Genuss. Wir mussten unsere nächsten Schritte in Chile planen und mit den Ideen von Bolivien beginnen, dann mussten wir einen ersten Zeitpunkt für die EU haben und was ungefähr passiert und wann. Diese einjährige Reise ist komplizierter, als ich zunächst dachte. Lots zu planen und zu organisieren, auch wenn Sie es nicht ALLE planen wollen.

Der letzte Tag in Bariloche wurde mit einer wirklich touristischen Fahrt mit einer Gondel auf den Cerro Otto verbracht. JA, ich fuhr die Gondel hoch und runter. Es war mental sehr schwer für mich. All diese Dinge zu tun und zu wandern, und ich kann kaum einen Fuß vor den anderen stellen. Wir waren überrascht zu erfahren, wo das REAL Original der DAVID-Statue wirklich gesät wird. Auf Cerro Otto. Nein, wirklich nicht

KAMERAD . Ich habe Mate in diesem einen Monat in Argentinien schätzen gelernt. Nicht, dass es jetzt mein Lieblingsgetränk ist. NEIN. Aber ich verstehe zumindest einige der Dinge, die in den guten Kumpel gehen und was es gut und schlecht macht, wie man es trinkt, wie man es zubereitet,…. zumindest ungefähr. VERKNÜPFUNG

Der Ausflug in den Norden nach Mendoza, die Dessert- und Malbec-Region war die nächste.

Es wird unser letzter Tag in Argentinien sein. Wir sind in einer kleinen Vorstadt namens Chacras. Es ist etwas südlich von Mendoza und kein Ort, den ich normalerweise besuchen würde, aber es war gut als eintägiger Zwischenstopp auf dem Weg nach Chile.

Ich habe ein paar Werkzeuge benutzt, um das Wetter zu finden und den Weg zu finden.

- Clima.com APP ist detailliert und schien mir zuverlässiger als Wunderground.
- Die Website windguru.com war bei weitem die beste Vorhersage, was in den nächsten Tagen passieren wird. Die Schnittstelle ist etwas gewöhnungsbedürftig. Es sind viele Daten zu verdauen.
- Maps.me APP ist eine gut entwickelte Offline-Karten-App, mit der Sie Daten speichern oder das Ziel ohne Internetabdeckung finden können. Das einzig Negative daran ist, dass der Karte eine Reihe von Orten fehlt, die uns interessiert haben.

Nous sommes restés à Bariloche pendant une semaine. C'était la haute saison pour la région. Nous voulons louer une voiture.   • Die Website windguru.com war bei weitem die beste Vorhersage, was in den nächsten Tagen passieren wird. Die Schnittstelle ist etwas gewöhnungsbedürftig. Es sind viele Daten zu verdauen.
  • Maps.me APP ist eine gut entwickelte Offline-Karten-App, mit der Sie Daten speichern oder das Ziel ohne Internetabdeckung finden können. Das einzig Negative daran ist, dass der Karte eine Reihe von Orten fehlt, die uns interessiert haben.

Nous sommes restés à Bariloche pendant une semaine. C’était la haute saison pour la région. Nous voulons louer une voiture. Vous l’aurez deviné, finies les voitures des magasins de location internationaux et locaux. Ensuite, notre hôte BnB intervient et joue ses relations. Voilà, nous avons une voiture pour 3 jours. Cela nous a permis de faire les deux voyages dans la région des lacs, comme je l’ai déjà décrit. Vraiment beau. Ensuite, le Circuito Chico et l’incroyable configuration de la brasserie Patagonia. Puis je suis tombée malade d’un rhume et je me suis sentie terrible, faible et tout ce jazz. Mumu et moi avons réussi à sortir nos mégots de toute façon pour aller sur le sentier que je voulais faire. Refugio Del Frey. J’ai réussi à faire environ la moitié de la distance et nous avons dû faire demi-tour, Mumu était prêt à faire beaucoup plus. Le vent a traîné au niveau du lac. Le parc semblait bien entretenu et offrait de superbes vues sur les lacs et la région. Nous sommes retournés au studio et j’ai plutôt fait une sieste… .. Quelle perte que de ne pas l’avoir parcourue comme je l’avais prévu.

Nous avons vraiment aimé pouvoir cuisiner pour nous-mêmes et manger ce dont nous avions besoin, pas ce que quelqu’un a mis au menu. La stabilité, c’est nécessaire dans notre vie et je continue de réaliser à quel point j’en ai besoin. Les formalités matinales habituelles pour se rendre au grand café Derilante et déguster leur bière étaient un vrai régal. Nous avions besoin de planifier nos prochaines étapes au Chili et de lancer les idées de la Bolivie. Nous devions ensuite avoir une première échéance pour l’UE et ce qui allait se passer et quand. Ce voyage d’un an est plus complexe que je ne le pensais initialement. Lot à planifier et organiser, même si vous ne voulez pas tout planifier.

Le dernier jour à Bariloche a été consacré à une excursion vraiment touristique à Cerro Otto avec une gondole. Oui, j’ai monté et descendu la gondole. C’était très dur mentalement pour moi. Toutes ces choses à faire là-bas et faire de la randonnée et je peux à peine avoir un pied devant l’autre. Nous avons été surpris d’apprendre où est réellement semé le véritable original de la statue de DAVID. Au sommet de Cerro Otto. Non vraiment

CAMARADE . J’ai appris à apprécier Mate pendant ce mois en Argentine. Non pas que ce soit ma boisson préférée maintenant. NON. Mais au moins, je comprends certaines des choses qui entrent dans le bon compagnon et ce qui le rend bon et mauvais, comment le boire, comment le préparer,…. au moins grossièrement. LIEN

Le voyage vers le nord jusqu’à Mendoza, la région du dessert et du Malbec était le suivant.

Ce sera notre dernier jour en Argentine. Nous sommes dans une petite ville de banlieue appelée Chacras. C’est juste au sud de Mendoza et ce n’est pas un endroit que je visiterais normalement, mais c’était bien comme une escale d’une journée sur le chemin du Chili.

J’ai utilisé quelques outils pour la météo et trouver notre chemin.

  • Clima.com APP est détaillé et m’a paru plus fiable que Wunderground.

  • Le site Web windguru.com était de loin la meilleure prédiction de ce qui se passerait les prochains jours. L’interface est une chose à laquelle il faut s’habituer. C’est beaucoup de données à digérer.

  • Maps.me APP est une application de carte hors ligne bien conçue qui vous enregistre des données ou vous permet de trouver votre destination sans couverture Internet. Le seul inconvénient, c’est qu’il manque un tas de lieux qui nous intéressaient sur la carte.
Yves and Dominique - a few days with friends in SJ
